News.title: Daughter's horror after 'bones of British mum and dad' killed in wildfire found inside car after funeral
News.content:
Daughter's horror after 'bones of British mum and dad' killed in wildfire found inside car after funeral

Danielle Gillam-Kirton said police told her there was nothing to see inside the burnt-out car that her parents died in - but claims she has now found their bones

View 2 Images Pete and Fran Gillam died in their car after being caught in wildfires in Spain

The daughter of a British couple who died in the Spain wildfires claims she has discovered their bones - despite already having 'cremated' their remains.

‌



Pete and Fran Gillam died in their car after flames tore through Bédar in the Almería province on July 9. They were among 14 people, including seven British nationals, who died after 40C temperatures sparked devastating, rapid fires that swept across the countryside and devastated two towns.

‌



Danielle Gillam-Kirton, 42, claims that Spanish police previously told her that the vehicle was so burnt out that no items were found inside, other than a small fragment of bones that were cremated at a funeral service this summer.

‌



But after going to the wreckage site herself, she said she immediately found multiple bones inside the car, along with keys, jewellery and change. The discovery has sparked serious doubts over whether the car was ever properly searched by officers, and where the bones they were originally given came from.

View 2 Images A total of 14 people died when fires rapidly spread across Almeria (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

Describing the moment she peered inside the car and found a hip bone, Danielle told the Guardian: "I honestly can’t describe what that felt like. I remember staring at what was in my hand, and the slow realisation of what I thought I was looking at hit me. I shouted out in shock."

‌



She said the ordeal has compounded the grief already felt by the family, and left them wondering: "Who or what did we cremate?"

The newly-found bones have now been sent off for DNA testing, a development Ms Gillam-Kirton said only came after repeated pleas to local authorities, who had initially dismissed the findings as animal bones.

Later assessments suggested the bones are human, she said.

‌



Ms Gillam-Kirton, who previously criticised what she said was a lack of proper warnings issued to people in Almería on the day of the tragedy, wants the Foreign Office back in London to put pressure on the local police for answers.

The Mirror has contacted the Foreign Office for comment.

Amid questions over whether more could have been done to prevent their deaths, families of the 14 victims in Bédar are currently considering whether to launch a private prosecution against the local government, reported Spanish media.

Article continues below

This would give them direct access, through their lawyers, to judicial files detailing how prepared the country was for a major wildfire of the type seen in Almería.

The emergency mobile phone alert system was never activated during the fires.

Regional officials said that the rapid-moving nature of the fire and the limitations of the technology when it comes to targeting small areas meant that the notifications could have prompted confusion, blocking off vital routes for emergency services.

News.title: Paddington fire LIVE as trains to Heathrow Airport cancelled
News.content:
A blaze is causing 'major disruption' in London this evening with all lines between Paddington and Heathrow Airport currently blocked

A fire near a train track near Paddington station has caused major disruption for travellers this evening, as services to Heathrow Airport have been cancelled.

London Fire Brigade said six fire engines and around 40 crew members are on the scene after a fire broke out near Scrubs Lane in North Kensington just after 4.10pm today (Saturday, September 5).

The blaze is said to have caused an electricity supply failure, causing all lines between Paddington and the airport blocked, National Rail has said in a statement.

Cancellations and delays to services are expected until at least 7.15pm, with disruption expected until 9pm this evening, it added.

News.title: MIKE TAPP: 'Protest is fine but not like this - intimidating ordinary people in Dover is last thing town needs'
News.content:
MIKE TAPP: 'Protest is fine but not like this - intimidating ordinary people in Dover is last thing town needs'

Labour MP for Dover Mike Tapp says he will be asking police questions after hundreds of balaclava-clad men descended on the port town, with many chanting "stop the boats"

View 2 Images Mike Tapp MP was frustrated by the protest in Dover (Image: Philip Coburn /Daily Mirror)

Protest is fine. But not like this. Hundreds of men dressed in black and wearing balaclavas descended on Dover and blocked roads into Britain’s busiest ferry port.

‌



They chanted about small boats while stopping ordinary people getting to work, disrupting businesses and holding up families trying to start their holidays.

‌



They rather missed the mark.

‌



Dover knows better than most the pressures immigration and border disruption can bring. We have lived on the front line of the small-boats crisis for years. We have also endured queues and gridlock caused by changes to cross-Channel travel.

So the last thing Dover needs is another group deliberately blocking our roads.

View 2 Images Protestors blocked ferry passengers from reaching the port (Image: @Ay_audits/YouTube)

‌



Motorists left in fear after masked protesters storm Dover READ MORE :

The Port of Dover is not just another road junction. It is critical national infrastructure, handling around a third of UK trade in goods with the EU and huge volumes of roll-on, roll-off freight. When Dover stops, Britain feels it.

And the law matters. Wilfully obstructing a highway can be a criminal offence. New legislation also means police can designate protest areas where concealing your identity with a balaclava or other face covering becomes an offence.

But policing depends on preparation. This was clearly organised, yet Kent Police appear to have had little advance warning. I will be asking why, whether intelligence was missed, and whether additional officers - including mutual aid from forces such as the Met - can be mobilised quickly enough when Dover is targeted again.

Article continues below

There is another irony.

Small-boat arrivals this summer were down 46% compared with last year. Government action is starting to work: stronger cooperation with France, more disruption of smuggling gangs, more arrests and more returns.

People have every right to protest about immigration. They have every right to demand stronger borders. But intimidating a town in balaclavas and blocking one of Britain’s most important ports? That isn’t the way to do it.

News.title: Motorists left in fear after masked 'stop the boat' protesters storm Dover and block port roads
News.content:
Motorists left in fear after masked 'stop the boat' protesters storm Dover and block port roads

Protesters began arriving in the Kent town at 7am with traffic blocked and ferries delayed

View 3 Images Around 300 men in balaclavas stormed Dover (Image: / SWNS)

Motorists told how they were left in fear as a mob of masked protesters stormed Britain’s cross channel port today.

‌



Around 300 men, dressed head-to-toe in black, blocked a key road to the Dover crossing while chanting “stop the boats” and “whose streets? our streets”.

‌



It is believed the balaclava-clad horde was orchestrated by Patriotic Platform, a far-right group founded by convicted criminal and xenophobe YouTuber Danny Tommo.

‌



Ferry passenger Toby Mackenzie was petrified when his car was surrounded. He wrote online: “Pretty much left me fearing for my life. Happy that I didn’t drive through them to protect myself. Generally fearing for my life.”

View 3 Images Protestors blocked ferry passengers from reaching the port (Image: @Ay_audits/YouTube)

Reform conference sees woman hit on head with crutch and hair pulled in sickening clip READ MORE :

Reform plunged into chaos by donations row as Nigel Farage heckled during major speech READ MORE :

P&O Ferries were delayed for up to an hour, with passengers who missed their sailing offered alternative slots.

‌



Traffic on the A20 was stuck in four mile tailbacks, causing delays of at least 45 minutes to reach the port.

Frustrated travellers slammed the demo. One wrote online: “Was stuck on a boat in Dunkirk for over an hour and a half, which also means I will miss my hospital appointment for a potential life-threatening illness this afternoon. Stop the boats? Wrong ones!”

Lania Tkaczyk, who was staying at the town’s Premier Inn, said: “We were stranded this morning and have only just been able to leave. It was quite intimidating seeing the men head-to-toe in black.”

‌



Kent Police later revealed no arrests had been made in the “spontaneous protest”.

Appearing to take credit for the action, Tommo, a friend of far-right activist Tommy Robinson – real-name Stephen Yaxley-Lennon – shared footage and posted: “It’s time! Protect our country! And more importantly our women and children! This is our warning!”

He previously said his aim is to create “a patriotic army that is able to take control of the United Kingdom”.

‌



Robinson also posted: “Simultaneously at different locations across Dover patriots have mobilised to close down the port.”

Nick Lowles of anti-racism charity HOPE not hate said: “Since the riots of 2024, Tommo has repeatedly spoken about the need to take to the streets and take direct action.

“Despite warnings from HOPE not hate, the authorities have failed to act – they’ve allowed him to agitate, organise and mobilise large groups around the country. Today is clearly the consequence of the inaction from the police and we fear that without decisive action things will only get worse from here.”

‌



View 3 Images Ferry passengers faced lengthy queues (Image: / SWNS)

Protesters began arriving in the Kent town at 7am. Traffic coming in and out of the port was blocked. By lunchtime, police had moved the crowd away from the port area and guided them toward the Dover Priory railway station.

Some locals leaning out of flats waved and applauded as they marched past.

‌



Labour MP for Dover and Deal Mike Tapp, a former soldier, said: “I am fed up with idiots coming to Dover to cause disruption. Go home. Enjoy your weekend, get a job.”

In 2016 Tommo, 37, admitted attempted kidnapping and was sentenced to two years in prison after taking part in an armed attempt to abduct a man during a drugs-related dispute.

And this year he became involved in direct action around Dover, targeting migrants arriving by small boats.

Article continues below

He pleaded guilty last month to entering a restricted area of the harbour in March without lawful authority.

A government spokesman commenting on yesterday’s events said: “The right to peaceful protest is fundamental to our democracy, but we condemn the behaviour in Dover and the travel disruption it has caused.”

News.title: Rare trio of Pacific cyclones form as El Nino creates perfect storm conditions
News.content:
Rare trio of Pacific cyclones form as El Nino creates perfect storm conditions

Cyclones Lowell, Karina and Marie have all been spotted in the Pacific – the first time three hurricanes have been simultaneously active in the Eastern or Central Pacific since 2015, as El Niño fuels rare weather conditions

View 2 Images A satellite image of Earth shows the storms forming

An extraordinary trio of tropical cyclones has been spotted swirling over the Pacific Ocean.

‌



Rising temperatures in the Eastern Pacific, driven by El Niño, have created the perfect breeding ground for these powerful storms to form.

‌



El Niño is a weather phenomenon in which sea surface temperatures in the tropical eastern and central Pacific climb above their long-term average, typically occurring every two to seven years.

‌



Warmer ocean waters pump more heat and moisture into the lower atmosphere, reducing air pressure and enabling thunderstorms to organise themselves into spinning tropical cyclones.

Cyclones Lowell and Karina are expected to reach category 3 or 4 intensity, while Marie could approach category 3 strength.

‌



View 2 Images Lowell is forecast to pass close to Hawaii next week

UK's El Nino problem as Brits set for extreme winter and food shortages possible READ MORE :

Lowell is forecast to pass close to or just west of Hawaii as a major hurricane early next week, while Karina and Marie are predicted to stay over open water, posing no direct threat to land.

The last occasion three hurricanes simultaneously churned through the Eastern or Central Pacific was back in 2015, when Hurricanes Kilo, Ignacio, and Jimena all spun across the Pacific during another El Niño year.

Article continues below

Category 3 and 4 hurricanes are classed as major storms, packing sustained winds of at least 111 mph (178 km/h) and capable of wreaking havoc, including widespread power cuts and extensive destruction of trees.

News.title: Reform UK conference: Nigel Farage desperately tries to downplay donations row in closing speech
News.content:
Reform UK's conference descended into chaos after Scotland Yard said it was assessing reports that senior figures sought to evade electoral law over donations

Reform UK's crisis-hit conference has finally come to an end with an underwhelming speech from Nigel Farage.

The Reform UK leader - who lost two of his top aides during the three-day gathering - claimed it had been an upbeat event despite the donations scandal overshadowing the conference.

His keynote speech on the main stage yesterday was beset by chaos after he was interrupted by multiple hecklers. Security teams dragged out protestors as disorder ripped through the conference.

Robert Jenrick lost his cool this morning after being asked about the allegations facing Reform. The rattled Reform Treasury spokesman accused a TV presenter of wanting to “waste the interview talking about tittle tattle” and dismissed the undercover sting - that forced two Reform aides to step down - as a report by “some pranksters".

Reform faces the possibility of investigations by the police and the Electoral Commission into the report by Channel 4 News and Verbatim Investigations.

Mr Farage has tried to downplay the secretly-recorded comments as "loose pub talk" and said Reform won’t be distracted by a "campaign of attacks". He insisted Reform has “broken no laws” and had not “taken any dodgy money”.

This live blog has now closed.

News.title: Krystian Bielik appears to grab young Portsmouth fan by the throat during Cardiff City chaos
News.content:
Krystian Bielik appears to grab young Portsmouth fan by the throat during Cardiff City chaos

Portsmouth's 2-0 win over Cardiff City at Fratton Park on Saturday was marred by unsavoury scenes after Krystian Bielik allegedly clashed with a home supporter

View 3 Images

Cardiff defender Krystian Bielik allegedly grabbed a young Portsmouth fan by the throat during an angry clash in Saturday's Championship game between the two sides.

‌



The altercation happened midway through the second half of the match, which Portsmouth won 2-0. Bielik had headed over to the touchline to try and retrieve the ball for a throw-in, only to become embroiled in a heated clash with a young home fan.

‌



Replays of the incident, which quickly went viral on social media, allegedly show the 28-year-old grab the supporter around the throat. The Pompey fan retaliated by directing what appeared to be a slap at Bielik. The game was briefly paused while the referee attempted to restore order.

‌



The supporter was later ejected from the stadium following the incident. Bielik, who was booked earlier in the game, escaped further punishment, though it is likely The FA will investigate the incident, with Bielik potential facing a lengthy ban and a significant fine.

View 3 Images The clash occurred when Bielik went to retrieve the ball

View 3 Images

‌



On the pitch, goals from Conor Shaughnessy and Marezi Marezi did the damage for Pompey, who move into midtable.

Defeat at Fratton Park means Cardiff are without a win this season; they have drawn three of their five league games since winning promotion and drop into the bottom three.

Cardiff boss Brian Barry-Murphy said of the incident post-match: "I wanted to make sure he (Bielik) was protected and make sure he was okay, which he is.

‌



"I thought the referee and his staff handled the incident impeccably. I was assured by him the correct processes will take place.

"He said he’d seen everything which occurred really clearly, so he diffused the situation and implemented the correct processes from there.

‌



"The players are always subjected to different things that’s not acceptable. My job is to protect the players, but really I’m trying to make sure that we play well and win.

"I’m sure the FA will look at it and implement the correct processes."

News.title: King Charles and Queen Camilla enjoy Braemar Gathering ahead of Andy Burnham meeting
News.content:
King Charles and Queen Camilla enjoy Braemar Gathering ahead of Andy Burnham meeting

The King and Queen were greeted by thousands of spectators at the famous Highland Games event before travelling to Balmoral to meet Prime Minister Andy Burnham

View 2 Images King Charles and Queen Camilla during the Braemar Gathering (Image: © 2026 PA Media, All Rights Reserved)

The King and Queen basked in Highland sunshine at the annual Braemar Gathering before hosting a meeting with the Prime Minister.

‌



Charles and Camilla received a warm welcome from thousands of onlookers at the celebrated Highland Games event prior to heading to Balmoral to meet Andy Burnham.

‌



Sunshine pierced through the clouds and the countryside burst into life as masses descended upon the venue in the heart of the Cairngorms National Park, famed for its royal connections.

‌



A variety of competitions were on display, from cross country racing and tug of war to caber tossing, the high jump and Highland dancing. Spectators stood to welcome the royal pair before the national anthem rang out.

Pipers and drummers received thunderous applause from attendees as they paraded around the games arena.

‌



View 2 Images Charles and Camilla enjoyed the games before a meeting at Balmoral with Andy Burnham (Image: © 2026 PA Media, All Rights Reserved)

The Queen received a heather posy from 11 year old Highland dancer Ally Dey.

Master of ceremonies Robert Lovie declared during the royal entrance: "We are greatly honoured that your majesties have graced us with your presence today, which enriches this gathering and all that Highland Games and culture represents, and I know I speak for everyone – both in your beloved Royal Deeside and from the family of Highland Games officials and competitors – in sending you both our warmest and most loyal good wishes.

Article continues below

"Today, in the fine autumnal splendour of this Highland village, we present the finest of athletes, sportsmen and women, dancers, pipers and drummers and a proud showcase of talent from your majesty's armed forces."

News.title: Disruption at Port of Dover as masked 'stop the boats' protesters block roads
News.content:
There has been major disruption at the Port of Dover due to a large group of masked men holding a demonstration.

Hundreds of protesters, dressed in black and wearing face coverings, blocked roads and were heard chanting "stop the boats".

Traffic was stopped from going in and out of the port, with the government saying it condemned "the behaviour in Dover and the travel disruption it has caused".

Kent Police, which made no arrests, described it as a "spontaneous" protest, while Mike Tapp MP said questions need to be asked around why it appeared the police "didn't know about it".

Officers moved the crowd from the port to Dover Priory railway station at about 11:30 BST and said "all involved had dispersed by 12:00".

Paul King, Reform UK councillor for Dover West, said he had been told it was a "stop the boats protest".

Kent Police has not yet commented on who was behind the demo.

Far-right activists Tommy Robinson and Danny Thomas both posted about it on X, praising those involved.

Thomas is believed to be the founder of the Patriot Platform network.

Anti-hate organisation Hope Not Hate claims that Patriot Platform arranged the protest, saying the group began meeting in July and has brought together members of anti-migrant groups from around the country.

Demonstrators told the BBC they did not want to talk to the media, although one said "send them back" and another said "stop the boats" when approached.

News.title: Nigel Farage tells BBC he 'wasn't listening' during foreign donor talks filmed undercover
News.content:
There's no question the allegations in the Channel 4 film have been embarrassing for Reform, and disrupted what they hoped would be a conference about their plans for office if they win the next General Election.

Everywhere around the huge, draughty exhibition hall in Birmingham are giant posters and placards saying, "Reform - the first 100 days".

They wanted to herald their deal with a serious contender to be the next French President, Jordan Bardella, to deal with small boats.

They were keen to highlight the promise to cut income tax if they win the election, scheduled to be in 2029.

They wanted to talk about their proposals for education, welfare, planning, and the rest.

Party members, delighted to have a reason to get together, have taken part in those sessions, applauded and cheered in the hall; gone wild for Farage on stage.

But for the rest of the country, most of the noise from the conference will have been the huge and awkward story about the toxic mix of politics and money.

What is harder to assess is the impact this mess will have on Farage's standing with the public, after a tricky summer and a recent poll slump.

At the top of the party there is a quiet admission that what has happened here is a genuine mistake.

One senior figure told me they could brush off other claims of murky funding, confident nothing had gone wrong - but they conceded these claims do matter, and that for a certain vital percentage of voters, it would "cause them to ask questions".

No one is pretending it's just what Farage tried to joke was a "little, local difficulty".

And there is a private acknowledgement that stories like this can be off putting to voters beyond Reform's no doubt very enthusiastic base.

Another party source told me they were "totally blindsided" by the revelations; stunned "there'd just been no diligence" and in disbelief at how Jukes and Orr, who both say they'd done nothing wrong, seem to have behaved.

A different member of the party's top team said, "hopefully, it's just growing pains". In other words, Reform's developed so fast that sometimes mistakes are made. But they told me: "The party has to step up â sometimes the people that got us here, aren't the people for the next stage".

Among Farage's fans at the conference, I found different views. One member was convinced the party is treated unfairly: "It's the blob, it's all against him," she said.

But another young Reform enthusiast rejected that, telling me: "It's all documented and there on camera â Nigel has to be more careful about what party members say."

But there is a sense of "here we go again". When I asked another member what they thought of the financial scandal, a weary answer, "Which one?"

This time last year in the same conference complex, Reform felt like they were simply sweeping all before them. Twelve months on, they are having to work harder, the scrutiny is more intense, and the pressure only growing.

Farage's claim that he "wasn't listening" to the conversation was telling â to get to power without more of these kinds of serious embarrassments, he may have to pay more attention to what is going on.

News.title: Chris Mason: Reform UK winded by donations row as insiders call for shift in approach
News.content:
Defections, those who leave one party and join another, have been a big part of the party's growth in the last year â not least the recruitment of former Conservative cabinet ministers Robert Jenrick and Suella Braverman.

Elections have been as well - Reform's gains in the English local elections and the devolved parliament elections in Wales and in Scotland.

But so too has money. The backdrop to this conference was the swirl of questions about money even before Channel 4 News', and Verbatim Investigations', endeavours.

In the hour or two before its broadcast on Thursday night, senior Reform figures, including those directly caught up in it, projected a sense of being relatively relaxed about it. Awkward, embarrassing, but survivable.

Once it was broadcast, things changed. There was fury, I am told, and very quickly there was a sense of its gravity. "A few bottles of red were had, and we knew we had to act," is how one source described it to me. The conversations went on into the early hours.

Firstly, there was anger that it would drown out a conference that has been months in the planning. And yes, it has dominated conversation here in Birmingham.

Secondly, there was widespread concern about the image it projected, the impression it would leave.

Reform wants to project itself as ready to run the country.

Some saw James Orr's work as head of policy as key to that professionalisation. Orr as well as Dan Jukes, a close aide to Nigel Farage, have been suspended and both deny wrongdoing.

"We need people to see the reality that Reform is getting ready for government," I am told.

And yet the headlines allow critics to claim they are not just ramshackle and amateurish but can point to what looks like a pattern of activity, consciously pursued, to breach the law.

Absolutely not, Nigel Farage insisted to me, there was no such pattern.

But what of the ethos of the party? Journalist Tim Shipman in The Spectator writes , externalthat "it is the experience of everyone I have ever known near the summit of politics that political operations take their character and operating logic from the person at the apex of the triangle. Leaders set culture."

There is something in this. Take Rishi Sunak's Downing Street operation and Boris Johnson's. They were wildly different culturally, reflecting the very different characters at their helm. Would all the things that happened during Partygate under Johnson have happened under Sunak? Unlikely, I would have thought.

Some within Reform, who are full of admiration for Nigel Farage's chutzpah and gift as a communicator, are desperate to see a behind-the-scenes cultural shift that minimises the chances of further embarrassments. And, alongside that, a step up in the infrastructure and personnel to match.

Farage's team express frustration that this is precisely what they have been doing, but some are telling them internally they need to move more quickly.

Both Orr and Jukes will be missed profoundly by those inside the party.

Privately, some wonder if Orr may yet return.

Jukes, who has been a pivotal and loyal figure in Team Farage for years, was already dividing his time between the UK and the United States as his wife and baby are on the other side of the Atlantic.

Perhaps, some senior figures suggest, his immediate future might be in America. Does he return when the general election is nearer? Let's see.

Reform leave Birmingham winded and wounded by the last few days, their days in the sun overshadowed.

The question is how they deal with this and respond to it, in the coming weeks and months.

News.title: Jaguar Land Rover confirms planned job cuts
News.content:
Car manufacturer Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) has confirmed it is opening a voluntary redundancy programme, a year on from a cyber attack which brought production to a halt for more than a month.

The firm said it needed to save about Â£1.7bn over the next two years as it seeks to adapt to "evolving global market conditions".

It was reported by The Times on Saturday that as many as 4,000 jobs may be lost due to the impact of tariffs and a drop in sales.

The firm told the BBC it had not confirmed the numbers. It said the decision to cut jobs was to help "simplify" the organisation as well as "improve efficiency and build greater resilience".

"Today, we informed our colleagues, and trade union partners that JLR is opening a voluntary redundancy programme offering salaried and management team members the opportunity to leave the business," a spokesperson said.

"We will share further information with our colleagues first."

Unite general secretary. Sharon Graham. said the union had been warning about a "perfect storm" hanging over the automotive industry for some time.

"Death by a thousand cuts has been going on under the nose of successive governments," she said.

She added there had been "intensive" discussions over the weekend about mitigating jobs losses adding that she and Business Secretary, Jonathan Reynolds, would be meeting JLR's chief executive, PB Balaji, next week.

"This is an incredibly worrying and stressful time for JLR workers," said Unite national officer, Des Quinn. "Unite is working round the clock to deliver the best possible outcome."

News.title: Major disruption as grass fire halts all trains to Heathrow Airport
News.content:
Trains to and from Heathrow Airport have been halted after a trackside grass fire caused delays and cancellations.

National Rail said "major disruption" was expected until the end of Saturday following the incident which began shortly after 16:00 BST.

A statement said all lines were blocked between London Paddington station and Heathrow's terminals, as well as Reading, due to "a failure of the electricity supply caused by a fire next to the track".

It comes hours after a separate grass fire on Heathrow's airfield shut a runway earlier on Saturday.

Pictures on social media showed crowds of stranded passengers at Paddington, one of London's main rail hubs.

London Fire Brigade said six fire engines and around 40 crew members were tackling the blaze near Scrubs Lane, North Kensington.

Great Western Railway, external cancelled its services to Reading and no Elizabeth line or Heathrow Express services were running between Paddington and Heathrow on Saturday night.

The airport advised passengers to leave extra time for their journeys, adding that the Piccadilly line, which runs services to the airport, also has delays.

Earlier on Saturday, Heathrow's southern runway was closed while crews tackled a grass fire on the airfield.

It caused some disruption with at least two flights diverted elsewhere. Heathrow apologised for any disruption and said the fire was extinguished quickly.

That comes weeks after another grass fire near Heathrow's southern runway which forced 18 flights to divert and destroyed a large area of grassland.

While weather has cooled across much of the UK in recent days following record-breaking heat over the summer, fire crews have still been warning of wildfire risks.

The Met Office's Fire Severity Index, external shows that if a wildfire was to occur, it would have a "high" fire severity in most of south-east England and some of the Midlands.

The fire severity is "exceptional", the highest level on the index, in some parts of London including Heathrow, as well as on the Essex and Suffolk coasts.

News.title: Counterfeit weight-loss jabs are booming - and doctors are worried
News.content:
Excitement around the creation of a new drug, especially one showing early promise in clinical trials, is often celebrated by those developing it.

But new weight-loss drug retatrutide has become a headache not only for Eli Lilly, the pharmaceutical company behind it, but for regulators in the UK and around the world.

The jab has not yet been approved for human use by any regulatory body.

But illicit, counterfeit dupes of retatrutide are currently flooding the black market.

Experts have told the BBC this is one of the first times they have seen copycat versions of an experimental drug, still in the throes of being tested, become so widely available.

Vials purporting to be "reta" as it's become known, are being sold in the UK in gyms, nail and beauty salons, hairdressers, on social media and even by flower sellers on the street.

"The world has gone mad," pharmacist and director of 24 HR Pharmacy, Sehar Shahid says. "People are effectively injecting an illegal drug and thinking it's safe.

"It's become so normalised people openly talk about their dealers, where's best to get it from and post all over social media."

One quick flick through my socials and I can order a batch of a drug billed as retatrutide in minutes - although I would have no proof what it's actually made of, what its effects would be and where it's come from.

Keen users are posting before and after "reta" pics on their TikTok feeds, describing how it has silenced food noise, helped them shed pounds and lose inches, with some saying it's completely transformed their lives.

The problem? Despite positive results in its most recent clinical trials, real retatrutide is still being tested for its safety and efficacy.

Only 50% of drugs in this Phase III stage of testing in the US are eventually approved by the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), so there is no guarantee retatrutide will ever hit the market. The high rate of failure is primarily down to drugs not working as well in large, diverse human populations as they do in smaller early tests, or because they reveal unexpected safety hazards.

And the current, fake versions available may not resemble what's being developed in the safe confines of the laboratory.

News.title: Trump's response is key as Argentina's Falklands demands get louder
News.content:
Domestic politics can rarely be ruled out of the equation when the Falklands issue flares back up. However, Buenos Aires argues that the matter has become urgent: "A clear and urgent danger", as Milei put it.

With two energy companies â the Israeli-owned Navitas Petroleum and Rockhopper Exploration from the UK â due to undertake work on the Sea Lion oilfield off the Falklands coast within two years, the issue has new impetus. Argentina "cannot allow" the companies to "appropriate the oil reserves under our sea", he said. "We will not stand by with our arms folded," he added.

On Saturday morning Milei's office said on X that it was launching sanctions proceedings against 45 people and companies. The announcement did not identify those targeted and it is not yet clear what impact they will have.

In his speech, Javier Milei painted Argentina as a reliable and "trustworthy partner" to Washington and he enjoys Trump's support, both ideologically and personally.

The two men are close allies in a vision of the Western Hemisphere which Trump calls the "Don-roe Doctrine", a play on words on the 19th Century 'Monroe Doctrine' which exerted American domination over the continent. In essence, the two presidents want to see only like-minded leaders in power in the Americas.

Within such a new partnership and a reordering of the spheres of influence, it's more than conceivable that Trump favours the Argentine leader over the British Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, even if the issues at play transcend personality and party politics.

Perhaps the key question for the coming months, then, is whether the strength of the so-called "Don-roe Doctrine" outweighs the lasting history of the "Special Relationship".

News.title: Why the USS Lincoln turned up in Thailand looking so rusty
News.content:
When the USS Abraham Lincoln docked in Thailand this week some people were quick to criticise the condition it was in.

The US aircraft carrier has been at sea for about nine months where it's been supporting the US-Israel war with Iran.

BBC Verify has spoken to military experts who say, although the length of its deployment is unusual, the wear and tear isn't. Jake Horton reports.

Produced by Kevin Nguyen and Blanca Estrada. Graphics by Leo Scutt-Ritcher.

News.title: King and Queen join Highland games fans at Braemar Gathering
News.content:
King Charles and Queen Camilla have joined cheering crowds watching Highland games events at the annual Braemar Gathering in Royal Deeside.

The event, which draws spectators from around the world, is held on the first Saturday of September every year and coincides with the monarch's annual summer holiday at nearby Balmoral.

Among the events watched by the spectators were tug-of-war, caber tossing, hammer throwing, Highland dancing and a parade of pipe bands.

This is the fourth Games that the King has attended since his coronation.

News.title: Lauryn Hill, Wyclef and Giggs among surprise guests at Jay-Z's long-awaited UK show
News.content:
Jay-Z's first headline solo show in the UK in more than a decade saw him celebrate hip-hop culture alongside a host of special guests, including Lauryn Hill, Wyclef Jean and Giggs.

The US rap superstar rolled back the years for more than two hours - playing hits like 99 Problems, Empire State of Mind and Dead Presidents - as he took to the stage at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Friday night for the first of two shows in London this weekend.

The run is part of his Jay-Z 30 tour, which is marking the 30th anniversary of his debut album, Reasonable Doubt, and his culture-shaping career that followed.

Fans of his wife BeyoncÃ© had hoped she would join him on stage, like she did at two of his three New York shows this summer, as she was also celebrating her 45th birthday on Friday.

News.title: UK support for Falkland Islands 'unwavering' after Argentina restates claims, No 10 says
News.content:
It is not yet clear how or to what extent the sanctions will be imposed or tightened. In Argentina, a current law already allows for restrictions of activities of oil companies participating in projects considered unauthorised on the islands.

Two oil companies â Britain's Rockhopper Exploration and Israel's Navitas Petroleum â are due to begin extracting oil in the Sea Lion oilfield off the Falklands coast within two years, something Milei said Argentina could not allow.

A joint statement from the two firms on Friday said it had the valid licences granted by the government of the Falkland Islands, "and with the full support of the UK government."

The project is due to deliver its first oil in 2028, Rockhopper and Navitas said the partnerships' timetable would not be affected.

The Sea Lion oilfield, around 130 miles from the islands, contains an estimated 1.7 billion barrels of oil - described by Rockhopper as a field containing "highly marketable crude".

Milei also announced plans for a naval base in Tierra del Fuego in the south of Argentina, saying Trump and the US were "assessing their historical position in regard to the Falklands", which Argentina refers to as Las Malvinas.

"That is not empty words as they understand that Argentina is a reliable partner and a valuable ally for decades to come," he said, describing the UK as a nation "in decline".

On Thursday, President Trump hinted the US would not help the UK in any future Falklands conflict because Britain "had not been there to help me" during his war with Iran.

Trump's latest remarks on the islands come after he previously said the US position on the Falklands is one of many under review.

On Friday, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said the UK would "resolutely uphold" the self-determination of the islands.

Writing on X on Friday, Miliband said the Islands would remain British as that is the "overwhelming position of the islanders."

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting also said Britain's commitment to the Falkland Islands was "absolute and unshakeable".

"Milei's statement overnight tells us more about domestic politics in Argentina than it does about the Falkland Islands," he wrote in his own post on X.

In an earlier statement, Downing Street said it was "not the first time" the Argentine government had made economic threats against the Falkland Islands.

"We are clear that the Falkland Islanders' right of self-determination extends to the right to exploit their own natural resources," it said.

Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch said "Britain does not surrender to bullies".

"If (Milei) wants a stronger Argentina, he should build its economy, not threaten others."

Although the US is formally neutral, Washington provided support for Britain's campaign to retake the islands after the Argentinian invasion in 1982.

Argentine forces landed on the Falklands to stake a territorial claim in 1982, sparking a 74-day war over the territory as a British military task force ejected them.

The conflict led to the deaths of 255 British military personnel, three islanders and 649 Argentine military personnel.

In a sign of the ongoing tensions between the two countries over the issue, Argentina players celebrated their victory over England in the World Cup by waving a banner in support of their country's territorial claim.

News.title: Police probe after child dies in woodland
News.content:
A police investigation has been launched following the unexplained death of a child in woodland.

Emergency services were called to reports of a child in cardiac arrest on land near Strawberry Lane, Cheslyn Hay, Staffordshire, at about 08:45 BST on Saturday.

An air ambulance was sent to the scene, but the child was pronounced dead by paramedics a short time later, Staffordshire Police said.

The force, which has not confirmed the age of the child or any other details, is currently treating the death as unexplained.

Roads in the area were closed throughout the day while investigations took place and officers were expected to remain at the scene throughout the evening.

News.title: Cleveland police chief proud of force but being 'let down' by funding
News.content:
A Volkswagen Passat carrying five young men drove the wrong way down the motorway near Middlesbrough in the early hours of the morning before colliding with a marked police car.

Officers had been pursuing the car for almost seven minutes after it was connected to earlier alleged criminal activity, but the pursuit was abandoned 10 seconds before the crash when the Passat turned on to the dual carriageway, the Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said.

Fuller, whose force covers an area of north-east England that includes Middlesbrough and Teesside, recalled being asleep when the duty commander rang her with the news.

"No matter how tragic and devastated you feel, we swing into action and we do what we need to do," she said.

The home secretary announced this week that Cleveland Police would be given an extra Â£2m to deal with the fallout from the crash, with 200 officers drafted in from elsewhere.

Fuller told the BBC on Friday that she was grateful for the support the force had been given, but added: "I need that all the time."

Cleveland's Labour police and crime commissioner has previously said the force needed an extra Â£20m a year to hire more officers and crack down on organised crime.

Cleveland Police is grappling with the highest recorded crime rate of anywhere in England and Wales, Office for National Statistics (ONS) figures for the year to March show.

It also ranks highest for burglary, sexual offences, violence with injury, and criminal damage and arson.

Fuller said Cleveland Police had also experienced the largest decrease in the number of officers since 2010 and was staffed as if it were a rural force.

"It absolutely needs to change," she said.

Fuller expressed hope that reform to policing across the country was on the horizon, and that Cleveland Police would become one of the "big, strategic forces that have the resource, the flex and the capability to surge when they need to surge".

She added: "In the meantime, we need additional funding... to take us to that point."

Recent inspections show Cleveland is one of the most improved forces in England and Wales, with performance levels also judged to be some of the best in the country.

The force has recently arrested 87 people for offences linked to organised crime gangs and over the past two years 16 people have been jailed for such crimes.

Fuller denied that gangs had control over parts of Middlesbrough, describing it as a "complex" area to police, with high rates of school absence, drug addiction and mental health issues.

"We're doing the very, very best with what we've got - and we absolutely do need more."

Authorities say high deprivation and unemployment in the area are fuelling organised crime.

"When young people have little aspiration or hope, who don't have confidence in the state, then unfortunately criminals exploit these people," Fuller said.

"They give confidence, and they give them hope, and they give them aspiration. And sadly what that means is young people doing things without thought of consequences."

News.title: 'I'd rather die than ring the police': Distrust and fear in Middlesbrough after A66 crash
News.content:
All but one of the residents who speak to us do so on the condition of anonymity. They are worried that showing their faces could place them or their homes at risk.

What message do the attacks send to people on this street, I ask one.

"Well, they should be scared, shouldn't they, that something's going to happen to their property if they say anything or get involved. So we don't."

Victoria, who moved here several years ago, says the escalating violence cannot be separated from the wider condition of the town.

"This is a social problem, especially in this area. Teesside has been massively neglected and ignored," she says.

The attack in Acklam is far from Middlesbrough's only recent case of a vehicle being used as a weapon. Back in May, a tractor was driven into a house on Priory Road, and since the A66 crash Cleveland Police has investigated at least two further rammings.

Detectives have also linked their wider investigation to a caravan fire on Attlee Road in Grangetown.

"It's getting worse," a nearby resident says. "They're always balaclava-ed up as well, do you know what I mean?"

He blames drugs.

"It can't be anything else. Why would you be like you are unless it was drugs?" he says.

Whether every incident is part of a single feud has not been established. But taken together, the rammings, fires and arrests have created a powerful sense that violence is being used to intimidate, punish and send messages.

What is most unsettling for these residents is the sense that nobody is fully in control.

Grangetown and South Bank are communities still living with the void left by the decline of heavy industry. Both now rank among England's most deprived neighbourhoods.

In South Bank, we see a group of teenagers tend three ponies tethered on the grass. Two perform wheelies on electric scooters while another uses a long stick to scatter rubbish.

On the adjoining estate, more than a dozen homes have boarded-up windows.

On a wall are the words "RIP 2UZZI", said locally to have been the nickname of Jakub Matusiak, who lived one street away.

One 17-year-old boy tells us he knew him. "He was my best mate," he says. "It's sad."

Elsewhere, three letters are repeated: "FTP" - an expletive directed at the police.

I ask the teenager if he would call the police if another young person approached him carrying a knife.

"No," he says. Before adding: "I've never needed the police in my life. I'd rather die than ring the police."

Again and again, the young people we speak to express a profound distrust of the police.

Cleveland's Chief Constable Victoria Fuller said what we'd heard was "horrifying".

"Yes, there are a small minority of people in the Grangetown area who blight those communities. But we will continue relentlessly to serve our communities."

The scale of the challenge facing the force and the community it serves is not new.

The area has some of the highest police-recorded crime rates in England and Wales.

Its leaders have been warning for years that its resources did not match the demands placed upon it.

But recent inspections show Cleveland is one of the most improved forces in England and Wales, with performance levels also judged to be some of the best in the country.

The force has recently arrested 87 people for offences linked to organised crime gangs and over the past two years 16 people have been jailed for such crimes.

Since the crash, more than 200 additional officers have been deployed in Middlesbrough and surrounding communities. Their immediate task is to suppress the violence and identify those directing it.

There is also the question of restoring order and rebuilding trust and confidence.

News.title: New police team to crack down on illegal number plates across England
News.content:
A centralised crackdown on illegal number plates will target organised crime groups and drivers who dodge fines by bringing together data and information from police forces across England, the government has said.

The newly-created National Roads Policing Coordination Centre (NRPCC) will see improved collaboration across forces as well as new technology, such as specialist goggles that can detect number plates that have been made unreadable to cameras.

Illegal number plates are often used by organised crime groups to move stolen goods and to evade speeding, parking and clean air zone penalties, the Department for Transport (DfT) said.

Drivers with incorrectly displayed or missing number plates can be fined up to Â£1,000.

Illegal number plates can come in many forms including cloned plates - which copy the registration of a legitimate vehicle - and ghost plates - where a transparent film is used to make them undetectable to cameras.

Vehicles that hide from number plate recognition cameras are harder for police to track down when they are stolen or linked to crimes.

Policing and crime minister Sarah Jones said: "Illegal number plates are not a victimless offence.

"They are used by criminals to avoid detection, move illegal goods and stay one step ahead of law enforcement."

She said by bringing forces together and making better use of technology the new team would track down offenders faster and disrupt gangs.

Ch Supt Marc Clothier, deputy national co-ordinator for the NRPCC, said: "The police forces involved in our ghost plates operation have shown how effective a targeted and intelligence-led approach is in tackling offenders as well as educating and supporting drivers in ensuring their number plates are compliant."

News.title: Reform promises to increase tax-free personal allowance to £15,000
News.content:
Reform UK is promising to increase the tax-free personal allowance to Â£15,000, if it wins the next general election.

Robert Jenrick, the party's economic spokesman, has pledged to introduce the tax cut within the first 100 days if he became chancellor saying it would provide "money that people really need right now".

It is seen by Reform insiders as the flagship policy announcement of its conference and perhaps their biggest tax policy between now and the general election.

Asked about two senior Reform aides being investigated by the party following a Channel 4 News undercover broadcast into claims about funding, Jenrick told the BBC Nigel Farage had acted swiftly and they had been suspended.

In undercover filming by Verbatim Investigations Farage's senior aide Dan Jukes and Reform's head of policy James Orr suggested a way around electoral law to secure foreign party donations for the party, one of which would have totalled Â£500,000.

Electoral law sets out that to be a donor to a UK political party you must be a UK registered voter, or a company registered in the UK.

Farage said on Friday that his party had "done nothing wrong" and had taken "no illegal money. In fact no money was taken at all."

Jukes denied wrongdoing and said he was stepping away from politics "in order to clear my name". Orr told Sky News he would cooperate fully with the party's internal investigation.

Orr is an associate professor of Philosophy of Religion at Cambridge University's Faculty of Divinity, and responding to the Channel 4 News and Verbatim report, Cambridge University said it was "looking into these matters".

Jenrick told the Today programme that the party had taken legal advice and it did not believe it had done anything wrong.

Labour and the Liberal Democrats have reported the party to the Metropolitan Police.

The Electoral Commission has said it is considering "all relevant information, in line with our regulatory remit" and was in contact with the police.

Home favourites and former US Open finalists endured a terrible day on Saturday as all three of Amanda Anisimova, Madison Keys and Taylor Fritz lost in the third round.

Last year’s runner-up Amanda Anisimova lost in straight sets while Keys squandered a match point in a three-set loss and Fritz, the 2024 finalist, lost from two sets to love up against Francisco Cerundolo.

2017 finalist Keys saved five match points in her previous match, winning a thrilling deciding-set tiebreak, but there were no signs of that astonishing fightback as she instead collapsed in remarkable fashion against Qinwen Zheng.

The Olympic champion won the final seven games to beat the 22nd seed 1-6 7-6(3) 7-5.

Keys raced to a 5-0 lead in the final set and had match point on her serve at 5-1 but after failing to convert it momentum swung dramatically, leaving the American smacking her head with her racquet.

Zheng, who has slumped to world No 121 after an elbow injury which required surgery, had to come through qualifying to reach the main draw, but has previously enjoyed success in New York, reaching the quarter-finals twice.

She said: “I’m just telling myself keep holding every single point, never give up, stay there and somehow little by little it just happened.

“The hard work pays off.”

open image in gallery Zheng dropped to the court in joy as she overcame Keys ( AP )

Earlier on Saturday Anisimova lost 6-2 7-5 to 24th seed Anastasia Potapova, who was born in Russia but now represents Austria.

10th seed Anisimova, who has also been on the comeback trail this year after a wrist injury, was the picture of misery as she fell in the third round for the third grand slam in a row.

She converted just three of her 16 break point chances while 25-year-old Potapova surged ahead to equal her best performance at a major.

Later on Saturday Fritz fell 6-3 6-4 3-6 4-6 4-6 to 24th seed Cerundolo, spurning three break points at 4-3 in the final set before immediately falling a break down.

The Argentinian, playing his first match on Arthur Ashe Stadium, kept his cool to serve out the match from 0-30 down in his next service game, winning from two sets down for only the second time in his career.

Cerundolo said: “In the third I started to get into it, step by step, and in the fourth and fifth I played really good tennis. Taylor is a top player, he’s played in the final here, so winning, my first time on Arthur Ashe, it’s fantastic. I hope you enjoy, I know I’m not the local one, sorry, I try my best, hopefully I can get you all on my side in the next one.”

News.title: Katie Taylor vs Flora Pili LIVE: Croke Park fight start time, undercard, updates and results tonight
News.content:
Barry Keoghan stars in Katie Taylor video before boxing icon retires

Katie Taylor will bring down the curtain on her staggering boxing career tonight, as she fights one last time.

The Irish icon – an Olympic gold medalist and two-weight undisputed champion – will finally realise her dream of boxing at Dublin’s iconic Croke Park, as she faces the unbeaten Flora Pili.

Yet tonight’s main event is less about the result, which will crown an undisputed super-lightweight queen, and more about celebrating Taylor.

The 40-year-old is widely seen as the greatest women’s boxer in history, having played a pivotal role in bringing the sport to the Olympics, after getting her own start by pretending to be a boy.

Whatever happens tonight, Taylor’s legacy is secure, but this evening’s action will be must-watch regardless. Follow live updates and results from Taylor vs Pili and the undercard, below.

Amy Hunt continued her excellent season with second place in the 100m at the Diamond League Final in Brussels, edging former world champion Sha’Carri Richardson in a photo finish.

The Brit finished in 11.06s with Richardson a fraction of a second back in 11.07s, but no-one came remotely close to Jamaica’s Tina Clayton, who shot off the blocks as if rocket-powered and won her first title in 10.93s.

It brought an end to a successful weekend for 24-year-old Hunt, who also took third in the 100m on Friday night.

But there was to be no more success for Britain’s Georgia Hunter Bell, who looked tired throughout the 1,500m and faded badly in the closing straight.

open image in gallery Hunter Bell was fourth in the 1,500m ( Reuters )

It has been a brilliant season for Hunter Bell, who took Commonwealth gold in the 800m before European gold in the 1,500m, but she admitted before the race in Brussels that she was tired after a long season and she could not replicate her heroics from earlier in the summer.

Poland’s Klaudia Kazimierska set a new meeting and national record with a stunning run in a world-leading time of 3:54.05, with Kenya’s Dorcus Ewoi finishing strongly to overhaul Australian Jess Hull for second.

Hunter Bell drifted through the field shortly after the bell but did not react as Kazimierska attacked from a long way out, and although she managed to come up onto Ewoi’s shoulder found she had no response as the front three accelerated away from her. She finished more than two seconds behind the Pole in 3:56.40.

Audrey Werro won the women’s 800m in a meeting record of 1:54.75, but was pushed all the way by Dutch star Femke Broeders-Bol, who nearly had enough to come round the Swiss in what was the closest of their duels this summer.

The 400m hurdles specialist finished second in 1:54.81, with Ethiopia’s Saida Tsehaye third in 1:57.57.

22-year-old Werro took to the front behind the pacemaker, with Broeders-Bol slotting in behind her and Tsehaye on her heels. The three stretched away from the chasing pack before Werro’s pace proved too much for Tsehaye, with Broeders-Bol attempting to come round in the home straight but unable to reel in her rival.

Kenny Bednarek of the USA ran 19.61s to win the men’s 200m in dominant fashion, with Olympic champion Letsile Tebogo well off the pace in fourth at 20.01s.

open image in gallery Masai Russell set a new meeting record but was made to work for it by Devynne Charlton ( AP )

Sinesipho Dambile was second in 19.89s with Makanakaishe Charamba third in 19.99.

Masai Russell reeled in Devynne Charlton after an electric start by the Bahamian in the 100m hurdles, with the American coming through to win in a new meeting record of 12.20s, while Charlton set a national record of 12.33s, prompting celebrations from both athletes.

Brazilian star Alison dos Santos produced an imperious performance in the 400m hurdles, winning in 46.70s to eclipse American Andre Phillips’ meeting record of 47.51, which was set on this day exactly 40 years ago and also in Brussels.

Enric Mas extended his lead of the Vuelta a Espana in a reverse result to the last time the race summited the Sierra de la Pandera, as Marco Brenner took his first grand tour stage win and only his third pro victory.

24-year-old Brenner was part of a four-rider group who got clear on the category-one final climb, chasing down a late flyer by Santiago Buitrago and passing him for the biggest win of his career.

“I think yes [it’s the best day of my career],” a beaming Brenner said. “I cannot really believe it yet, I wasn’t feeling super until now, not feeling like myself, struggling with some sickness early in the race and a crash.

“I really wanted to show myself and my teammates that I can be up there. On the final climb I could feel that I actually have the kick today, and in the end I started believing it. You live for days like today, I guess.”

Spain’s Mas lost time to rival and eventual champion Primoz Roglic when the race visited the Andalusian climb in the 2022 edition, one of two in which Mas has finished runner-up to the Slovenian.

But this time he added another 25 seconds to his lead over the four-time champion, accelerating away on the upper slopes on another day in which his Movistar squad got their tactics exactly right.

Roglic slipped to third overall, 2’10”, as Felix Gall - who could not be separated from the maillot rojo despite the Swiss rider’s best attempts - moved up to second, 2’06” behind Mas.

As expected all the drama came on the final climb of the day, Sierra de La Pandera, an 11.8km monster averaging 7.5% but with multiple sections - including towards the summit - of 15% and some hitting gradients of 17%.

The 154.5km stage from Jaen was the last major mountain stage of the second week, and as in previous days an enormous breakaway got up the road, with UAE Team Emirates-XRG rider Kevin Vermaerke the first to break clear.

The American attacked with 53km to go but his solo charge was brought to an end by Georg Steinhauser with 14km remaining.

The lead chopped and changed on the final climb until a final quartet was established, with Brenner reacting superbly to a late attack by king of the mountains leader Buitrago - despite being caught zipping up his jersey at the exact moment Buitrago launched.

open image in gallery Enric Mas extended his lead to over two minutes ( AFP/Getty )

Brenner bridged across quickly and edged ahead of him in the final kilometre, punching the air as he crossed the line.

The last time the Sierra de la Pandera featured in the Vuelta Richard Carapaz won the stage and his EF Education-EasyPost squad attempted to lead him out for more heroics this time around.

But Movistar wrestled back control, leading the peloton up the punishing slopes, until the Ecuadorian launched from a heavily reduced group of favourites. Only Gall, Mas and Roglic were able to keep pace with the former Giro d’Italia winner before he and Roglic were distanced.

Gall suffered a blow earlier in the stage as he lost a second key lieutenant in as many days: after Gregor Muhlberger abandoned during stage 13 Jordan Labrosse withdrew partway through stage 14, with the balance of power within the peloton shifting towards Movistar ahead of a difficult final week.

But the Swiss produced another fine climbing performance to leapfrog Roglic, a key move ahead of stage 18’s individual time trial, where Roglic is expected to gain significant ground on both Gall and Mas.

There were no other changes to the order of the top seven in the general classification, with Britain’s Oscar Onley remaining in fifth place and in the best young rider’s jersey, 5’44” behind Mas having lost another 1’15”.

The race continues on Sunday with a hilly 110km run from Palma del Rio to Cordoba, which has been shortened from the planned 189km route as a result of heat warnings in Cordoba, which is expected to hit highs of 40 degrees.

In the Tour of Britain Cees Bol won stage 4 in Leyburn as British rider Lewis Askey lost the overall lead to Tim Wellens; the Belgian leads him by 21 seconds going into the final stage.

On Saturday night, Katie Taylor bids farewell to boxing on what is sure to be an emotional evening in Dublin.

The Irish icon, 40, will finally get to realise her dream of fighting at the iconic Croke Park, and she will do so in a main-event clash with Flora Pili.

• Follow LIVE: Taylor boxes Pili in final fight of legendary career

For Taylor, the fight represents a chance to become a three-time undisputed champion. The Olympic gold medalist previously held undisputed gold at lightweight and super-lightweight, and it’s in the latter division that she will meet Pili this weekend.

open image in gallery Katie Taylor will box the unbeaten Flora Pili (right) ( PA )

Taylor (25-1, 6 KOs) will carry the IBF, WBO and WBA belts into the famous stadium, where a sold-out crowd of 80,000 will watch on, while the vacant WBC title is also up for grabs.

Pili, 29, will bring her own belt into the fight – the IBO strap – although that version of the world title is not always granted the same prestige as the other belts.

In any case, Pili will also enter this fight with an unbeaten record (12-0, 2 KOs), as she looks to pull off the upset in front of Taylor’s home crowd.

Does the French boxer stand a chance, though? Betway has her listed as a huge underdog at 10/1, while Taylor is 1/20, and the draw is 20/1.

Silvia Bortot is perhaps the only name of real note on Pili’s resume; in 2023, Pili won a split decision against the Italian, who has fought world champions Lauren Price and Mikaela Mayer in the last three years – losing to both on points.

Still, Saturday’s main event feels like it is less about the result and more about celebrating Taylor, who is widely deemed the greatest women’s boxer of all time.

Fighting at Croke Park remains the only major accolade left for Taylor to tick off, after she twice headlined against fellow great Amanda Serrano at New York City’s iconic Madison Square Garden.

Taylor’s first fight with Serrano even brought the first seven-figure paydays in the history of women’s boxing, while their middle bout – on the undercard of Mike Tyson vs Jake Paul in Texas – broke viewership records by reaching 50m households on Netflix.

open image in gallery Taylor will finally realise her dream of boxing at Croke Park ( PA Wire )

Taylor’s promoter Eddie Hearn said this week: “If Croker would have originally gone, ‘Yes, this is going to be massive,’ I would have gone, ‘wow’, and we would have done it. But it was like: ‘I don’t know.’ Blimey, if they’re not sure, do we really want to be gambling with these costs?

"People can deflate your spirit, which is quite unusual for me, but they did deflate my spirit a little bit over the years, because they made me question whether we could do it or if it would actually work.

“And I’m disappointed in myself, actually, that I allowed that to happen, because maybe we could have done it earlier. But then I didn’t have the confidence that I had going into it this time with [Irish promoter] Peter Aiken involved and the three Amanda Serrano fights [behind us].

“Croker helped out as well and they were fantastic in the end. But I never thought we’d do 40,000 tickets on a pre-sale. How many could we have done? I don’t know, maybe another 40,000, 50,000, 100,000?”
