Sports.title: From Monaco 'robbery' to shock pole - but can Gasly win Italian GP?
Sports.content:
Pierre Gasly felt he was "robbed" on Friday after losing his podium from June's Monaco Grand Prix but turned it around in the most remarkable fashion with pole position for the Italian Grand Prix.

Just one day after the FIA International Court of Appeal reinstated Gasly's pit lane speeding penalties, the Alpine driver hit back with his maiden Formula 1 pole.

It is one of the biggest shocks in the history of F1 and, six years after winning his only race to date, also coming at Monza, Gasly has the opportunity to avenge, what he feels, was a wrong judgement call on Friday.

"It's been nine years I'm in Formula 1, trying to, give my best absolutely every single weekend and it's not every time we get a car to fight for pole position," said Gasly.

"Today it was the case and, yeah, I'm really, really happy, really proud to have seized this chance and to make it work. It was a heck of a lap."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes driver George Russell reacts to narrowly missing out on pole position to Pierre Gasly during qualifying at the Italian Grand Prix

Did 'extra motivation' power Gasly to pole?

Gasly has always shown plenty of emotion in and out of the car but was furious after finding out McLaren and Red Bull's appeals of the Monaco race result led to the return of his two five-second time penalties for speeding.

In June, Alpine had successfully won a right of review that saw the penalties removed as they proved Gasly was not speeding due to an incorrect measurement of the pit lane distance.

Gasly told Canal+ that "we're being robbed" and "I don't think this is going to end here" while Alpine chief Flavio Briatore questioned the relationship between the reigning constructors' champions and a judge at the FIA's International Court of Appeal (ICA).

The ICA responded to Briatore's comments on Saturday and stated they are "confident in the soundness of the proceedings and the integrity of the judges".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player McLaren's Team Principal Andrea Stella was not happy with Flavio Briatore's reaction to the ruling which meant Alpine's Pierre Gasly lost his Monaco GP third place finish after his two time penalties were reapplied

Nevertheless it certainly fired Gasly up and he produced one of the best laps in his nine-year F1 career, admitting the situation regarding the appeal was "not nice" but something he tried to use.

"I try to use everything I can into something positive and, extra motivation, but I think I could have dealt without it this weekend. That's all I'll say," he said.

Alpine managing director Steve Nielsen added to Sky Sports F1: "When you think what the mood was in the camp when we got the result from Monaco, which honestly is going to annoy me for the rest of my life, it's a nice way to bounce back with pole position. It's lovely."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at closing stages of the qualifying at Monza as Pierre Gasly took pole

Several drivers congratulated Gasly on his pole, including George Russell who will start on the front row in Sunday's race.

Russell revealed he was playing chess with Gasly before qualifying and the Alpine driver also beat him in their game.

"We were actually finishing a game of chess about 15 minutes before qualifying and he beat me there, and I thought, 'Well, I think I'll beat you in qualifying,' and here we are, he's ahead of me again," he said.

"So, yeah, huge congrats to him. Pierre and Alpine have been super-fast even from Q1."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Pierre Gasly reacts to a shock first pole position at Italian GP

Can Gasly convert pole into victory?

Gasly's only win so far in F1 came at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix - one year after his close friend Anthoine Hubert died and now he has another unexpected chance for a second victory.

The Alpine has been very quick in the straights in Monza thanks to the benefit of a Mercedes power unit, but the team also have a low-drag car which is strong aerodynamically.

Monza is an energy-rich track, so there is expected to be different power unit deployment strategies at play which will lead to the yoyo style of racing we saw earlier this year.

It may give Gasly a chance to keep Russell behind, or stick with him if the Mercedes driver is ahead.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes driver George Russell reacts to narrowly missing out on pole position to Pierre Gasly during qualifying at the Italian Grand Prix

Asked by Sky Sports F1 whether he could win, Gasly said: "Why not? I can be sure I'll do everything I can tonight, coming prepared for tomorrow.

"The good thing is, I know what it looks like not having anyone in front of you on this track, so at least if there is a place to start on pole, I'm glad it's here."

With championship leader Kimi Antonelli starting at the back due to grid penalties, a win for Russell would see him make significant inroads into his 59-point deficit to his Mercedes team-mate.

"It's going to be an interesting fight with Pierre as well. I think they've got a car that's got some good straight-line speed, which will be nice for them in the race," he said.

"I don't really know where the fight is tomorrow, but, confident I've got the pace to go for the win."

Sports.title: 'He got done over by Max' - Wolff blames Verstappen for Russell losing pole
Sports.content:
Mercedes boss Toto Wolff has claimed that George Russell missed out on pole position for the Italian Grand Prix because he "got done over" by Max Verstappen during the closing stages of qualifying at Monza.

Russell appeared to be on course to live up to his status as pole favourite, but his final flying lap was compromised by Red Bull's Verstappen slowing down in front of him and his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli.

Mercedes had placed championship leader Antonelli on track in front of Russell to give the Brit a tow, due to the fact the Italian is serving penalties for exceeding his engine-part allowance for the season and was going to start the race from the back of the grid regardless of his qualifying position.

Russell still improved his time to go fastest but then had pole remarkably snatched away from him by Alpine's Pierre Gasly, who pulled off one of the biggest qualifying shocks in the sport's history.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Pierre Gasly claims Alpine's first pole in 17 years!

Asked by Sky Sports F1 whether something had gone wrong for Russell to miss out on pole, Wolff said: "Yeah, I think at the end where he got done over by Max in the final run when launching the lap.

"It was just much too close, and that compromised the lap time eventually and that lost pole position."

Russell: It was a mess with Verstappen

With having a tow from the car in front being crucial to delivering a fast lap at Monza, Verstappen sought to force another car in front after having lost touch with the McLarens ahead of him.

As Verstappen slowed down ahead of the final corner, Antonelli passed the Red Bull, while Russell remained just behind them.

While a tow is useful, being too close to the car in front for the entire lap can also have a negative impact on performance, which Russell felt was the case.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes driver George Russell reacts to narrowly missing out on pole position to Pierre Gasly during qualifying at the Italian Grand Prix

"We had a bit of a mess with Verstappen entering the lap," Russell said. "He wanted to go for the tow, Kimi was there as well, and I did my lap a second and a half behind Max, which wasn't ideal.

Asked whether Mercedes could have done anything differently to avoid the situation, Russell replied: "I think, no, everything was all looking fine, but then going into Parabolica, Max just slammed on the brakes, and he didn't want to be the lead car.

"So, it's just one of those things. You can't control what other people do. Kimi was there to give me the slipstream, which he did perfectly on the first run, but obviously with Max, I think it also made it difficult for Kimi to know what to do as well.

"So, it was just a little bit unfortunate. In hindsight, probably would have been better off not trying this, but we wanted to give it everything."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Pierre Gasly reacts to a shock first pole position at Italian GP

Despite his frustration at missing out on pole, Russell remains in with a strong chance of reducing his 59-point deficit to Antonelli at the top of the standings.

He told Sky Sports F1: "I'm feeling good. I think the key is just to have a clean start, a clean first lap.

"As long as I'm in the top three or four after the first few laps, you're still within a great shot to fight for victory. That's the goal."

Verstappen: My car was jumping like a kangaroo

Verstappen didn't address the final-corner incident after qualifying, but revealed his own pace had been compromised by damage to his car, causing it to jump "like a kangaroo".

"As soon as I went out for qualifying, something failed again on the car," Verstappen told Sky Sports F1.

"It's something that we are aware of, and it happens more often in the year, but it's just costing lap time in the low-speed where the car just starts jumping around a lot more than it should do. On the bumps, the kerbs, the car's not compliant anymore.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Oscar Piastri is given a three-grid place penalty for this Lawson block!

"I was actually very happy with the car in FP3 because we took a big step forward from yesterday. The car was in a much better window, and overall I think today it was in a much better window, and overall I think today it was in a much better window.

"But when you have no ride control and the car is just jumping around like a kangaroo, you can't be consistent. It's actually a bit of a shame to not optimise our performance.

The four-time world champion qualified sixth but will move up a place to fifth on the grid due to Oscar Piastri being given a grid penalty for impeding.

On his prospects for the race, he added: "We need to be able to change whatever the part is, because otherwise it's going to be quite tough to race like that."

Sports.title: Le Fee penalty rescues draw for Sunderland at Brentford
Sports.content:
Enzo Le Fee rescued a point for Sunderland after dispatching his late penalty to secure a 1-1 draw at Brentford.

The Bees broke the deadlock just before the hour mark thanks to Vitaly Janelt's well-taken effort into the top left corner, only for referee Thomas Bramall to point to the spot in the 82nd minute to penalise Keane Lewis-Potter for holding Wilson Isidor inside the box.

The full-back did not have eyes on the ball while making contact and after being confirmed by VAR, Le Fee stepped up to dispatch it into the bottom right corner.

"We can do better, I always look at us," Brentford boss Keith Andrews said in his post-match press conference.

"I wasn't bowled over with the officiating today, though, which I rarely say.

"I don't tend to go on about officials too much. I will talk myself into trouble but I didn't like the flow of the game; there were incidents where it was not under control."

A point marked a fair return for both sides in a game where momentum swung in favour of both teams at different stages of the contest.

Sunderland, who switched to a back five for this fixture, had started the better side and came close to an opener in the first half after Dan Ballard's goal was disallowed following a lengthy VAR review and Le Fee hit the post with a fierce strike from range.

"It is a shame," Regis Le Bris said after the game regarding Ballard's goal, which was ruled out due to debutant Kevin Danso being offside. "If you need four and a half minutes to make a decision, it means you are hesitating."

Half-time changes from Keith Andrews - replacing Michael Kayode, Mamadou Sangare and Dango Ouattara with Aaron Hickey, Yehor Yarmoliuk and Anthony - inspired fresh impetus going forward.

Their unbeaten start to the season continues but marks the second consecutive week the Bees have squandered a lead late on and were forced to settle for a point following the 1-1 at Leeds United last time out.

The key moments from the Gtech...

9: DISALLOWED! Ballard's opener ruled out due to Danso offside on debut

20: OFF THE POST! Le Fee strikes the post with emphatic volley

45: TRIPLE CHANGE! Andrews replaces Kayode, Ouattara and Sangare with Hickey, Yarmoliuk and Anthony

57: GOAL! Janelt scores the opener with well-taken effort into top corner

70: DISALLOWED! Anthony's tap-in ruled out for foul on Roefs

82: PENALTY! Le Fee scores equaliser after Lewis-Potter penalised for foul on Isidor

Andrews: We were off our usual levels

Brentford boss Keith Andrews:

"It had a lot in it, the game. In the first half, we didn't hit the levels we had. The way they played was very good.

"We were a little bit off it and in the second half we did the basics very well. It allowed us to have control and more territory; we looked more like us and got ourselves in front.

"There were then decisions that went for us and did not go for us.

"I knew it would be a very difficult game today. It was a proper game. If I am in the stand and watching from afar, it is what the Premier League is all about. Going toe-to-toe with a good team and good coach."

Image: Brentford's Vitaly Janelt celebrates scoring their side's first goal of the game during the Premier League match

Le Bris: We dominated but Brentford switched the momentum

Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris:

"First half, we were dominant and created four big chances in the first 30 minutes.

"We managed this part of the game but didn't score. It is always a big shame.

"They changed three players and it switched the momentum. They scored but the lads were still in the game.

"We know we are good when we are behind. The subs helped."

VAR dominates post-match discussions again

Sky Sports' Patrick Rowe:

A miss for both teams with VAR at the forefront of the post-match discussions once again.

Brentford boss Keith Andrews was right to criticise the flow of the game and the control Thomas Bramall had at times but zero questions can be raised about the penalty.

A greater emphasis is being placed on players who do not look at the ball, have both hands on their opponent, make no attempt to play the ball or commit sustained holding of their opponent.

Keane Lewis-Potter did all four in plain sight of match officials and VAR.

Sunderland, meanwhile, were also left with a bitter taste in their mouths regarding officiating after it took longer than four minutes to disallow Dan Ballard's goal in the ninth minute.

"It's a shame because if you need four and a half minutes to make your decision, it means that you are hesitating," Regis Le Bris said after the game.

"So it wasn't a decision for us. It is what it is."

An enthralling game where momentum swung both ways should leave us talking about in-game management, the finish of Vitaly Janelt and Enzo Le Fee's late equaliser. Instead, it's VAR again.

Sports.title: High-flying Hull maintain unbeaten start by holding off Aston Villa in stalemate
Sports.content:
It’s never dull in Hull, as the saying goes in these parts, and after just three games the Premier League is proving to be quite some ride for Hull City supporters.

Having embarrassed Manchester United here on the opening day and won at Coventry last weekend, this deserved point and clean sheet will have reinforced Sergej Jakirovic’s belief that his men can beat the drop.

You have to go back to Bolton Wanderers’ excellent start to the 2001-02 campaign to find a newly-promoted side who began the season with three straight victories.

The Tigers failed to emulate Sam Allardyce’s team here but they came closest to a winner as the Algeria winger Mohamed Belloumi hit the crossbar with a stunning second-half shot before Mohamed-Ali Cho and Oli McBurnie went close late on.

For Aston Villa, though, it was a tepid display which saw them fail to score for the third match running with Hull looking the more likely winners.

Ambition pulsed loudly at a sold-out MKM Stadium before kick-off as a huge amber banner inscribed with the words “‘One family, one dream” was paraded on the pitch. It said much for the togetherness that Jakirovic has fashioned within his squad and the connection with the club’s supporters during a remarkable few months in the Tigers’ history.

They belted out a rousing rendition of their adopted club anthem, the Elvis Presley classic “Can’t Help Falling in Love”, as the match got under way.

Desire was visible and audible in the stands and on the pitch – and not least in the Hull technical area where Jakirovic, who signed a new two-year contract on Friday, watched proceedings unfold.

Villa failed to register a shot on target when losing to Brighton and Arsenal in their opening two defeats, but they should have led here inside the second minute when Nicolas Jackson headed Ian Maatsen’s teasing left-wing cross wastefully wide.

Hull were unfazed and Ryan Giles’s low delivery almost found Oli McBurnie before an exquisite piece of skill from Belloumi almost carved Villa apart. Collecting possession on the right flank, the winger beat Ross Barkley twice, including a delightful nutmeg, before breaking clear.

His low cross was cleared, but it hinted at the possibilities on offer for the hosts.

In the 13th minute, Villa finally fashioned an effort on target this season as Barkley found George Hemmings but his low shot was comfortably saved by Konstantinos Tzolakis.

If Villa could not see off a newly-promoted side widely tipped for an immediate relegation this season, could they really consider themselves ready to start climbing the table?

In the 25th minute, Villa went closer still through a low strike from Barkley, which drew a fine fingertip save from Tzolakis, as Hull came under increasing pressure.

Eight minutes before half-time, Belloumi tried his luck from 25 yards but his effort flew straight into Zion Suzuki’s midriff.

Moments later, Regan Slater also unleashed from 25 yards but the save was again comfortable for Suzuki while Villa had a penalty claim ignored on the stroke of half-time when Jackson went down under Nobel Mendy’s challenge.

A neat passing sequence should have harvested a Villa goal in the 50th minute but captain John McGinn could only lift the ball harmlessly over Tzolakis’s crossbar.

Three minutes later, Villa went even closer as Hemmings outstripped the Hull captain, Lewie Coyle, down the left flank and showed intelligence to pick out Emiliano Buendía with a neat cut-back. Buendía should have buried the chance but he blazed wildly over, much to his disgust.

In the 65th minute, Hull went agonisingly close to scoring when Belloumi collected possession from a short corner and curled a stunning left-foot shot against the bar.

Villa always gave the inescapable impression they could move through the gears when the opportunities presented themselves – but there was a resilience to the hosts. That collective desire which carried them to promotion last season will be needed over the next 35 games if they are to defy the odds and beat the drop.

It was evident again late on when Hull substitute Lucas Herrington – on his 19th birthday – produced a vital block to repel Tyrone Mings’s shot as Villa threatened a winner.

Cho’s close-range shot was repelled by Suzuki before McBurnie failed to properly connect with Giles’s cross as Villa held on.

Sports.title: Haaland edges Manchester City past Coventry as Fernández sparkles on debut
Sports.content:
Enzo Fernández started for Manchester City after Nico O’Reilly’s back injury during the warm-up and sparkled, showing why the club paid a British-record-equalling £125m for the midfielder. The winner came courtesy of Erling Haaland’s 300th goal in club football and Fernández had a key part, feeding Antoine Semenyo, whose cross from the right was crashed home.

In the second half Coventry hammered away, but their wait for a first top-flight goal since Mustapha Hadji’s second in a 3-2 defeat at Aston Villa on 5 May 2001 goes on. The visitors did not like losing, but were heartened by holding the star-studded hosts to a slender win, though the bottom line is all three of their Premier League outings on their return have been defeats.

Frank Lampard said: “I don’t think we deserved to lose. I’m disappointed we didn’t get what we deserved – which was a point. We can walk out of here with our heads held extremely high.”

Enzo Maresca’s men have a maximum nine points so can be supremely satisfied. “Today was not a nice win, a bit ugly,” he said. “In the first half we deserved more goals – we scored one but could have scored one or two more.”

The manager said of Fernández: “The reason Enzo was on the bench [initially] was because he arrived only a few days ago. I know how frustrating it was for him in the last weeks but in the end he played some minutes and was quite good. Nico felt something in his back – not serious.”

Ayyoub Bouaddi, bought for £85m, was on the bench for the hosts, as Fernández lined up alongside Rayan Cherki in a 4-1-2–2-1 that had Semenyo and Iliman Ndiaye, another new home signing, stationed behind Haaland.

View image in fullscreen Enzo Fernández shoots on his Manchester City debut. Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters

Coventry, with Ethan Pinnock and Frank Onyeka replacing Caleb Yirenkyi and Loum Tchaouna from the XI that lost at home to Hull, could have taken the lead when Abdukodir Khusanov played the ball back to Gianluigi Donnarumma and it slipped under the goalkeeper’s boot, but the Italian scrambled it clear. The visitors should then have bridged the 25 years to Hadji when a Semenyo pass meant for Rúben Dias was intercepted by Taiwo Awoniyi. But when the striker ran in his radar failed, and the shot was pulled wide.

The longer Coventry stayed level the better their prospects. Cherki fed a galloping Haaland and he twisted and let fly, but Carl Rushworth’s save was equal to the shot. Then, dazzling Cherki footwork – after a pass from Fernández – was followed by an effort that struck a post.

The frame of the goal and Rushworth could do nothing to stop Haaland’s opener. This time Fernández curved a pass in behind for Semenyo, the right-winger spun the ball over, and Haaland did the rest.

This was 26 minutes in and Coventry were under siege. Fernández collected the ball along the right, looked up and aimed a cross for Haaland but it failed to beat the first man. Then Cherki, again in Fred Astaire mode, made space and saw an effort blocked.

Maresca wants his wingers to be more direct – utilising the pace of Ndiaye and Semenyo – and the tactic spun Coventry. So, too, did an impish Cherki flick which put Haaland in again: he rode a challenge when going down might have brought a penalty, before shooting. Rushworth once more thwarted the Norwegian.

View image in fullscreen Frank Lampard and the Coventry players applaud their fans but their wait for a Premier League goal goes on. Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters

For Coventry, Jack Rudoni did better than Awoniyi with a header at close range, but Donnarumma flew to his left to prevent an equaliser. This showed the hope Lampard’s men carried but they had to finish any chance as these were scarce.

Ndiaye was fairly quiet on debut and when Cherki’s work took the ball to him in the area he should have pulled the trigger but refused.

Maresca said of the Senegalese: “Ili just had two sessions with us – most of the time he was moving in the wrong way, he needs to learn. When Marc Guéhi has the ball [at centre-back] he was dropping a lot – we didn’t need that, we needed him in the final third, that space was for Josko [Gvardiol, the left-back].”

The manager was more enthused about Elliot Anderson. “Really impressed not just today, he was very good against Palace, and against Bournemouth,” said Maresca. “The best thing with Elliot is day by day he wants to be better.”

Bouaddi’s home debut came on 75 minutes for Fernández and the 18-year-old showed composure during Coventry’s late-game bombardment, which included Ellis Sims forcing a point-blank save from Donnarumma.

Sports.title: Glasner claims VAR was ‘guessing’ after Forest are denied winner against Spurs
Sports.content:
Oliver Glasner argued there was insufficient evidence to disallow Neco Williams’s goal against Tottenham, accusing the video assistant referee Peter Bankes of guessing that the Nottingham Forest defender handled and said ruling it out weakens the officials’ authority. Midway through the second half, Williams stooped to head in on the goalline as Sandro Tonali attempted to hook the ball clear after Morgan Gibbs-White’s deflected effort bobbled towards the net.

Glasner conceded at least one angle showed Williams appeared to handle the ball, seemingly to protect himself as Tonali went to clear the ball with his left boot, but said the footage was too unclear to disallow the goal. “I don’t think VAR can intervene when he’s guessing,” said Forest’s head coach. “It was not clear and obvious. We had a briefing before the season that the threshold for VAR intervention should be very high and this is why it was a wrong intervention for me.

“I’ve watched five or six different angles and to be fair, from one angle you can guess that the ball touched the arm because the shirt [of Williams] moves a little bit, but it’s not clear whether it’s [because of] the ball or Tonali on the goalline. I know refereeing a Premier League game is really difficult – refereeing a training session is sometimes really difficult – but we are told to support the referee, to keep the threshold for VAR intervention very high, to strengthen the referee’s decision and they didn’t do that today. With these kinds of situations, you weaken the referees.”

Bankes checked the goal and then the referee, Craig Pawson, took to the mic before awarding a Spurs free-kick amid a chorus of boos from the home support: “After review, the ball touches the hand of Nottingham Forest’s No 3 before the goal is scored.” Williams was adamant he did not handle the ball. “I headed it in between my arms,” said the Wales defender, who this week signed a new four-year contract. “If you’re going to pause it, it’s going to look like it hit my arm but it didn’t. I have seen all the images and at not one moment can you tell that has clearly hit my arms because it never. I knew straight away I’d headed it down in between my arms.”

The disallowed goal was undeniably the moment of an underwhelming contest. For the third successive league match, Tottenham failed to score and this time they did not even muster a shot on target. Dominic Solanke heading on to the roof of the Forest goal, 88 minutes on the clock, was as threatening as they got. Omar Marmoush wellied a shot wide after Spurs countered at speed. Mykhailo Mudryk was brought off the bench for his first competitive minutes for 645 days after a doping suspension but Spurs were blunt. Aside from a 5-1 win against a Charlton B team in the Carabao Cup, their season so far reads: five goals against and none scored.

View image in fullscreen Spurs’ Mykhailo Mudryk came on as a late substitute for his first competitive appearance for 645 days. Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/Reuters

Apart from Gibbs-White’s effort in the buildup to the disallowed goal, Forest’s only other shot on goal was a daisy-cutter from James McAtee. The Spurs league debutant Sávio, a £75m arrival from Manchester City, showed a few neat touches but he and Destiny Udogie were withdrawn after an hour on the advice of Tottenham’s medical department. “I’m not happy when we have the plan but it is for my advantage, my business, the management of the players after their injuries,” said De Zerbi, who accepted his team lacked quality in the final third. “We have to make better decisions, to keep more calm when we are very close to do something important.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

No wonder both teams remain winless. Spurs’s date at home to Everton next weekend has taken on another layer of significance and the same applies to Forest’s trip to Aston Villa. Vinai Venkatesham, the Tottenham chief executive in attendance, could be forgiven for wondering when Spurs will see the fruits of their £300m-plus spend, much of the focus on sharpening their attack. They turned to Mudryk, who thrived under De Zerbi at Shakhtar Donetsk, after the failure to sell Richarlison halted moves for preferred targets Cody Gakpo and Iliman Ndiaye. This was not the desired result. “We bought very, very good players but you can’t just build the team with the names like in Football Manager,” De Zerbi said.

Sports.title: Chilwell seals Crystal Palace comeback win after Mitchell double at Fulham
Sports.content:
The managers may have changed but the result stays the same. For the fourth successive trip to this part of west London, Crystal Palace returned over the river with a win as Pierre Sage got his reign off the mark in dramatic style. Their hero was Ben Chilwell, the former England left-back who was signed on deadline day from Strasbourg – this time permanently, after a loan spell in which he helped Palace win the FA Cup – after he came off the bench to volley home the winner.

It was a bitter blow for Fulham’s new manager Álvaro Arbeloa, who had seen his side lead twice through the impressive Josh King – who showed his potential in front of the watching England manager, Thomas Tuchel – and César Palacios before being pegged back twice by Tyrick Mitchell, the second in a moment of pure slapstick. Arbeloa and his side left the pitch to boos from some supporters and remain pointless after three matches. But having won here three times in 2025 under Oliver Glasner, this has been a happy hunting ground for Palace and Chilwell could not contain his delight as he celebrated with Sage and the travelling fans at the full-time whistle.

“Today’s lesson was free because we won but we were inefficient in buildup during the first half,” said Sage, who maintained his record of never losing three games in a row as a manager. “It’s really a difficult period for me because I don’t like the mindset of the team and the club in this moment because [the transfer market] is always open. I like to know who I will work with.”

View image in fullscreen Tyrick Mitchell equalised twice for Palace. Photograph: Tony O Brien/Reuters

Fulham, who had almost 65% possession and racked up 25 shots in total, had looked more likely to end their winless start until Mitchell’s second goal swung the momentum decisively in Palace’s favour. They have now conceded seven goals in their first three league matches and Arbeloa – who was managing Real Madrid a few months ago – knows they must improve before next week’s game to face Liverpool at Anfield.

“We lost a game that we didn’t deserve to lose. But in football you need to take your chances and they did that better than us,” he said. “We need to learn quickly because things can change when you concede a goal.”

It didn’t take long for Alex Iwobi – the 30-year-old who has become only the fifth player in Premier League history to play 100 or more games for three clubs – to start pulling the strings for Fulham in midfield alongside the new £30m signing from Southampton, Shea Charles. A sloppy early pass from Jaydee Canvot inside the first minute that almost handed Palacios an opportunity betrayed the nerves of a Palace defence that had the Chelsea loanee, Axel Disasi, in the centre of the back three also favoured by Sage’s predecessor.

View image in fullscreen César Palacios scored his first goal for Fulham to put them back in front before half-time. Photograph: Tony O Brien/Reuters

Fulham took the lead when Adam Wharton failed to clear a cross from Oscar Bobb and it fell straight into the path of King, whose shot took a big deflection to deceive Dean Henderson. It was typical of Sage’s luck in his first month at the helm that a superb apparent Palace equaliser less than two minutes later was chalked off. Daichi Kamada had strayed millimetres offside before volleying in a brilliant cross with the outside of his boot from Yéremy Pino.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The visitors could have found themselves 2-0 down when Henderson saved a Timothy Castagne shot from close range, but Mitchell beat Bernd Leno at his near post to equalise against the run of play after being set up by Eddie Nketiah. Palace’s joy was short-lived, however. Chris Richards – being watched by his USA manager Mauricio Pochettino – was fooled by King’s clever dummy and the England Under-21 midfielder accepted the invitation to burst into the box. His cross would have been diverted into his own net by Canvot had it not been for an excellent save from Henderson, but even that only left Palacios with the opportunity, which he accepted, to put the ball into the empty net.

Yet Palace’s fortunes suddenly changed for the better when they scored a comical second equaliser. Mitchell’s initial effort was cleared by Gonzalo García as the striker charged back into the area, but the Palace defender volleyed hopefully towards goal as he fell, and García somehow managed to miss the ball altogether as it trickled over the line.

Fulham seemed to shrink after conceding and Palace sensed an opportunity. The comeback was completed when Chilwell volleyed in after Anan Khalaili’s effort had been blocked, and Fulham were forced to accept their fate once more after their own substitute left-back, Ryan Sessegnon, found the sidenetting in injury time.

Sports.title: Enzo Le Fée penalty redemption rescues point for Sunderland at Brentford
Sports.content:
True redemption, perhaps, would have been to score with a Panenka, but Enzo Le Fée didn’t quite have the chutzpah for that. His duffed dink at Brentford in January was the low point of one of Sunderland’s two worst performances of the season, but he converted from the spot with eight minutes remaining to earn a draw in a battle of two physically aggressive and well-drilled teams who must both look at the chaos elsewhere and be thinking again of top-half finishes.

It had seemed that it would be a tale of Brentford’s newfound strength in depth and a second-half turnaround as they overcame a rocky first period to have the better of the second after a triple change at half-time, having already lost their captain Nathan Collins to a calf strain. But instead it was a Sunderland substitute who made the key contribution, Wilson Isidor being held by Keane Lewis-Potter at the back post to earn the penalty.

“The first half we didn’t hit the levels we have,” said the Brentford manager, Keith Andrews. “Second half I thought we did the basics very well, allowed us control and a little bit more territory. I think if we’d played the same XI second half there would have been a reaction, but we needed that chance for renewed energy and new personality. We need to constantly evolve and adapt according to what teams do against us. We feel confident we can fix different problems with the personnel we have.”

These are not normal times. Clubs up and down the Premier League are in flux, undercooked and struggling to deal with a flurry of late signings. In that context, it’s reasonable to wonder what the ceiling for Brentford might be. They narrowly missed out on Europe last season, but with this squad and rivals wobbling, a first qualification has to be the target this time round. Business done early and wisely, Brentford are the poster club for what now seems an old-fashioned model of team-building, one that doesn’t lead to flustered final day sprees or competing private jets on the runway at Lyon airport. They may rely on algorithms and the data-led unearthing of hidden gems, but there is at least a sense of a squad being built for footballing rather than financial reasons.

View image in fullscreen Vitaly Janelt controlled a bouncing ball well to give Brentford the lead. Photograph: David Klein/Reuters

The feeling with Sunderland is always that they’re rather more effective when there is no expectation that they will make the play. Countering dangerously, often through the erratic and unpredictable stylings of Nilson Angulo, they had the four best opportunities before the break: a Dan Ballard volley was ruled out because the debutant Kevin Danso was offside and in the goalkeeper’s eyeline, Le Fée smacked a shot against the post and, twice, goalbound efforts were blocked in the six-yard box, once by Jannik Schuster, who impressed after replacing Collins, and once inadvertently by Brian Brobbey, who got in the way of that rarest of things, an on-target effort from Noah Sadiki.

Sunderland’s manager, Régis Le Bris, said: “We were dominant but didn’t score, which is a shame when you come away somewhere like this. We still have this character. We are good when we are behind and we are still able to change the dynamic.”

Andrews called it a “proper game” and said tactical battles like that “make me feel alive”. And his half-time shake-up worked. Brentford looked far more comfortable after the break, and Igor Thiago had already headed a close-range chance straight at Robin Roefs when Vitaly Janelt put Brentford ahead after 57 minutes, meeting Nordi Mukiele’s diving headed clearance at the top of the bounce and steering a controlled slice into the top corner.

As Aaron Hickey, one of those three half-time changes, got much tighter to Angulo than Michael Kayode had, the Sunderland threat down the left diminished. Mamadou Sangaré, having dominated the 3-0 win over Spurs, found life rather harder against Granit Xhaka and Sadiki, but Brentford now have options on the bench. Yehor Yarmolyuk came on and imposed himself far more. Jaidon Antony, similarly, offered fresh impetus in replacing Dango Ouattara.

But while Sunderland’s lack of incision remains an area obviously in need of improvement, they had just about enough to haul themselves back into the game; those spurned first-half opportunities will not be rued too much.

Sports.title: Luka Vuskovic rides to the rescue for Brighton as Leeds fail to take chances
Sports.content:
What might have been; what should have been. By the end of this strange, enthralling match two exhausted teams trudged off the Amex Stadium turf wondering how they had not won it. Both sides’ ruminations were entirely legitimate.

Leeds, who remain unbeaten three games into the season, rued not putting the game to bed long before Brighton even remembered they, too, were allowed to attack. Having led through Jayden Bogle’s early tap-in, the visitors were utterly dominant for the best part of an hour, bullying their hosts and seeing a number of chances go to waste. By the time Brighton belatedly gained a grasp on things, Leeds’ xG sat at 2.5 and the hosts’ languished just above 0.1.

Yet once the ignition had been sparked, Fabian Hürzeler’s side skipped second gear and went straight to fifth. A Luka Vuskovic header with 19 minutes remaining set up an unlikely thunderous finish from the hosts, which left Leeds clinging on to a point. In all, Brighton managed an astonishing 17 shots after half-time, with their dominance ever increasing as the clock ticked down.

Asked what had changed in the second period, Hürzeler replied: “Everything. We had more intensity, more energy, won more personal duels, we were sharp to the second balls.

“We can change a game within two or three minutes; we have this quality. But we have to be consistent to not always chase the result, to not always come back from an easy goal for the opponent. We have to find answers because two completely different halves is not enough.

“We showed a lot of energy, created plenty of chances, plenty of occasions when we were really dangerous in the opponent’s box. But we definitely need to start better.”

Not since 2009, at the Withdean Stadium, have Leeds won a game at Brighton.Bogle’s goal was the first they had even scored in nine visits, stretching back to November 2012.

“Overall, a point away at Brighton is really good for us given our recent record here,” said the Leeds manager Daniel Farke. “But more is even possible. At half-time, we should have been out of sight.

“In the second half, of course they put pressure on us, but we didn’t allow many chances. But the pressure is mounting and if you don’t bury the game Brighton has enough quality to come back and score. But I loved that my players dug in.”

Those travelling back to Yorkshire will have replayed the abundant opportunities their side’s earlier dominance yielded. Dominic Calvert-Lewin was twice put through on goal in the opening half, initially dragging his shot wide (which prompted a late offside flag) and then rounding the goalkeeper, only for Lewis Dunk to slide on the goal line and halt his shot.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Jayden Bogle scores with a tap-in to put Leeds 1-0 ahead in the first half. Photograph: Dylan Martinez/Reuters

Anton Stach almost scored from close range immediately after half-time, and he then delivered a wonderful cross that Ao Tanaka turned past Bart Verbruggen, but the strike was ruled out after the Japanese midfielder had strayed a couple of inches offside. Tanaka had earlier smashed against the crossbar.

The only time Verbruggen’s goal was legitimately breached came after 15 minutes when Calvert-Lewin’s header was palmed out to Tanaka, who squared for Bogle to tap in from a yard.

Having averaged more than 70% possession in their opening two league games, Brighton again had the lion’s share, but took almost an hour to figure out how to do anything with it. Perversely, until that point they had seemed incapable of retaining the ball in key positions.

Following a smattering of half-time boos from the home contingent, the game transformed late on. Charalampos Kostoulas produced a wonderful jinking solo run, weaving his way past four men before sticking a weak effort into the hands of James Trafford, who then had to be at full stretch to turn a Malick Yalcouyé shot round the upright. Vuskovic’s headed goal came from Maxim De Cuyper’s corner, and suddenly Brighton were rampant.

Yasin Ayari curled an effort straight at Trafford, Promise David turned one over the bar, and Pascal Gross smashed too high when gifted a prime opportunity from six yards out. That they only scored once was a source of amazement. What might have been; what should have been.

Sports.title: European football: Nwaneri forces late own goal to cap dramatic Dortmund comeback
Sports.content:
Arsenal loanee Ethan Nwaneri caused a late own goal in Borussia Dortmund’s favour, as his side came from two down to win 3-2 at Hoffenheim in a topsy-turvy Bundesliga clash.

Hoffenheim were the better team for the opening hour but lost their way as Dortmund clicked into gear and romped to victory with three goals in the final 30 minutes.

Hoffenheim were two up with 54 minutes played thanks to goals from Leon Avdullahu and Tim Lemperle.

Nwaneri, who became the youngest player in Premier League history in 2024, arrived on a season-long loan from Arsenal on deadline day and came on with half an hour played after an injury for Filippo Mane.

Striker Serhou Guirassy gave the hosts hope when he scored just after the hour mark and then set up Fabio Silva five minutes later.

With just four minutes of regular time remaining, Nwaneri cut down the left and shot centrally, but his effort took a big deflection off home defender Albian Hajdari and into the goal.

Bundesliga newcomers Elversberg continued their excellent top-flight arrival with a 4-3 win at Borussia Mönchengladbach, making it two wins from two this season.

Gladbach took the lead twice and were 3-1 up midway through the second-half, but Elversberg fought back despite losing manager Vincent Wagner to a second yellow card just before the break.

With 10 minutes left, Felix Keidel levelled the scores at 3-3 and Maurice Krattenmacher put the visitors in front in stoppage time with his second goal of the match.

Bayer Leverkusen rebounded from their loss to Elversberg last Saturday by putting sorry Union Berlin to the sword in a 4-0 home victory.

Argentina internationals Equi Fernández and Facundo Medina had Leverkusen 2-0 up at half-time. England centre-back Jarell Quansah set up Patrik Schick for Leverkusen’s third before Ibrahim Maza added a stylish fourth late on.

West Ham loanee Niclas Füllkrug scored his second goal in three games since returning to Germany to help Werder Bremen win at home 3-1 against RB Leipzig. The Germany striker scored a long-range header, with Eren Dinkci and Marco Grüll also getting on the scoresheet.

Europa League finalists Freiburg continued their perfect start to the season with a solid 1-0 win away at promoted Paderborn.

Defending champions Bayern Munich face promoted Schalke later on Saturday.

View image in fullscreen Oihan Sancet roars with delight after scoring Bilbao’s third goal. Photograph: Vincent West/Reuters

In Spain, Athletic Bilbao thumped Atlético Madrid 3-0 on a miserable afternoon for Diego Simeone’s side. Nico Williams, Robert Navarro and Oihan Sancet’s goals gave the Basque hosts a resounding victory at San Mames.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Athletic secured back-to-back wins under former Borussia Dortmund coach Edin Terzic, after losing their first two matches of the campaign.

Striker Julián Álvarez, who tried to leave the club to join Barcelona this summer, returned as a substitute after illness but was ineffective in his second-half appearance.

On Sunday La Liga leaders Barcelona visit Valencia looking to move clear of Real Madrid, who lost 1-0 at Real Betis on Friday.

A late Ché Adams strike sealed a 2-1 comeback win for Torino over Fiorentina as the Florence club’s nightmare start to the Serie A season continued.

Mateo Pellegrino’s long-range strike put Fiorentina in front early in the second half, but a pile-driver from Rolando Mandragora – who had only joined Torino from La Viola four days earlier – drew the scores level.

Scotland international Adams sealed his side’s first points of the season in the 82nd minute, plucking a cross out of the air and flicking it in from close range to stun the Stadio Artemio Franchi crowd.

Fiorentina, the two-time Italian champions, have lost their first three games by an aggregate score of 9-1, and were booed off by their own fans following a performance that left them in last place.

Inter host Napoli in the early evening in a meeting between last season’s top two sides, before Gian Piero Gasperini faces his former club when Roma host Atalanta.

Sports.title: Own goal and inspired debut from keeper Akane Okuma earn Villa point at Chelsea
Sports.content:
A Veerle Buurman own goal punished a profligate Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, securing a point for Aston Villa in a frustrating start to the hosts’ push to win back the WSL title.

How Villa came away with a point having conceded 65% possession and having amassed just seven shots to Chelsea’s 34 and five touches in the opposition box to the home team’s 57 is somewhat inexplicable.

Chelsea were creative and Lauren James was at her free-flowing best, but they could not convert their many chances, and the new Villa goalkeeper Akane Okuma’s monumental performance was a big part of that.

“If you analyse the performance today and the statistics of the game you can say that’s crazy we couldn’t win the game,” said the Chelsea manager, Sonia Bompastor. “You need to make sure you kill the game because when you are only one-nil up, you are always exposed. That’s what happened today and I think at the end of the game we are all frustrated because it’s not a good result.”

View image in fullscreen Almost every Villa outfield player joined the celebrations for their equaliser. Photograph: Katie Chan/Action Plus/Shutterstock

Chelsea’s summer has been one of change after a somewhat transitional season that broke a run of six consecutive WSL titles, and spirits have been high about their potential. However, they have a problem up front: with the new signing Melvine Malard, who came off the bench and scored two in their Champions League qualifier home leg against Real Sociedad, out with an injury, and Mayra Ramírez yet to make her return from a long lay-off, Aggie Beever-Jones failed to make the most of the opportunity to lead the line.

“In football, some of these things are also about mentality and mindset when it comes to being ruthless, being critical in the box,” said Bompastor. “The best teams don’t need to have many opportunities. So, that’s something we need to work on and find solutions for.”

Ushering in a new era in front of 7,900 fans at Stamford Bridge, where they will play all their WSL home games for the first time, Chelsea’s aggressive and relentless pressing in the opening half-hour caused all sorts of problems for Natalia Arroyo’s team, forcing error after error.

View image in fullscreen Lauren James gave an early sign of what she is capable of with a finish that left the Villa keeper helpless. Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/Reuters

It was no surprise when that physical effort yielded results. In the 11th minute when pressure caused confusion between Okuma and the target of her pass out from the back, the loose ball was worked to James who glided into the box, shifting her weight as she went, before lashing the ball into the roof of the net. It was a statement goal from a statement player.

This was always going to be a tough opening game for Villa, who had lost all 12 of their previous WSL games against Chelsea and were starting five of their eight summer signings,. They only began to look a little more comfortable and structured as the home team’s pressure eased off towards the end of the first half.

“We just need to go through that and understand that when you’re in the middle of the jungle or whatever, at some point, you arrive at a point where there’s no more trees and I think that’s what we do at the end of the first half,” said Arroyo. “We get the energy back in the changing room and we talk about how to avoid these moments.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Chelsea’s profligacy in front of goal was the big frustration for Bompastor, and Villa were clinging on for large swathes of the game with Okuma, signed from the Japanese champions INAC Kobe Leonessa, key to keeping the margin to one goal.

View image in fullscreen Noelle Maritz’s (centre) shot led to Veerle Buurman’s own goal. Photograph: Katie Chan/Action Plus/Shutterstock

At no stage had it felt like the visiting team would be able to take something from the game. They were patient, but Chelsea were the masters of their own downfall, and in the 79th minute the ground was silenced when they failed to clear Lynn Wilms’ cross, Noelle Maritz swiped it goalwards from eight yards out, and Hannah Hampton’s block sent the ball bouncing off Buurman and over the line.

The home side pushed hard for the winner but Okuma was equal to every attempt. “We gave her some nice tests this week trying to know where she was at, if she was nervous, if she had any doubt and in which ways we could help her,” said Arroyo. “She’s still settling in here, she’s still trying to learn the language to be able to communicate with all the players, but we were surprised to see that she was safe in some of the actions, she read the game really well.”

On the final whistle the Japanese goalkeeper was enveloped in the hugs of her teammates as the players in blue digested how they had ended up with only a point from such a dominant performance.

Sports.title: Furious Roberto De Zerbi rips into Tottenham's misfiring £165m attack - as toothless Spurs continue wait for first goal of the season after another blank at Nottingham Forest
Sports.content:
Furious Roberto De Zerbi rips into Tottenham's misfiring £165m attack - as toothless Spurs continue wait for first goal of the season after another blank at Nottingham Forest

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Roberto De Zerbi took aim at his £165million strike force after Tottenham left Nottingham Forest still searching for their first goal of the season.

Spurs at least claimed a point at the City Ground yet for the first time since 1974, they have failed to score in each of their opening three games.

De Zerbi’s team did not register a shot on target against Oliver Glasner’s team and the Italian bemoaned his attackers’ poor work in front of goal.

‘In the last third we have to improve,’ De Zerbi said. ‘We have to improve and take better decisions, make keep calmer when we are close to doing something important in the final third.

‘When Omar Marmoush had a shot and it went over, we had Andy Robertson overlapping. If we had taken the right decision, Mohammed Kudus was at the far post waiting to score.

‘How many crosses did we send beyond the far post? Mathys Tel, twice. Savio, once. Tel has big potential but he takes too many wrong decisions.’

Tottenham's new-look £165million attack has yet to score a single goal so far this campaign

Savinho was hooked off on the hour mark as Tottenham drew 0-0 with Nottingham Forest

De Zerbi also revealed he had taken off Savio, making his Premier League debut following his £75million move from Manchester City, and Destiny Udogie on the advice of the club’s medical staff. ‘There was a plan not to take risks,’ he said. ‘I'm not happy. But football is like this. Savio has not the best physical condition to play 90 minutes. He's an important player for us, a crucial player. Destiny is another crucial player for us.

‘I think Kudus and Robertson, they played well. But it's not so easy to come in from the bench and adapt immediately.

‘I'm not happy when we have the plan, but it's for my advantage, for my business, the management of the players after injuries.’

Oliver Glasner became the latest Premier League manager to let rip at VAR after the technology intervened to deny him a first win as Nottingham Forest boss.

Neco Williams thought he had given Forest the lead midway through the second half when he bundled the ball home from close range. The goal was originally given by referee Craig Pawson but chalked off after VAR ruled Sandro Tonali’s attempted clearance had struck Williams on the arm before rebounding into the net.

Glasner did not believe Pawson had made a clear mistake and argued the goal should have stood.

He said: ‘I have watched it back to see all the angles, five or six different ones. From one angle, you can guess that the ball touched the arm as the shirt sleeve moves, but it’s not clear why.

‘So if we are guessing, VAR cannot intervene. It’s not clear and obvious and we were told before the season the threshold (for intervention) should be very high. We accept the point but it feels like we lost two.

Roberto De Zerbi took aim at his strike force and demanded improvements in the final third

Oliver Glasner was furious that VAR had chalked off Neco Williams' goal for a handball

‘Refereeing a Premier League game is really difficult. The right way to support the referee is to keep the threshold high. With these kinds of situations, you weaken your referees and everyone wants to support the referee as the job is not easy.

‘I told the referee I felt the goal should have stood but if he is called, he has to trust VAR. I’m sure all the Forest fans have the same opinion.’

Williams added: ‘It's a goal. VAR is there when there is a clear and obvious error and for me that is not clear and obvious. I've seen the images and the replays and at not one moment did I think I handballed it. I headed it in between my arms. If you're going to pause the replay, it's going to look like it hit my arm but it didn't hit my arm.’

Sports.title: Rangers captain Lawrence Shankland faces MONTHS on the sidelines after suffering hamstring injury in win over Motherwell
Sports.content:
Rangers manager Derek McInnes fears captain Lawrence Shankland is facing months out of action with a hamstring injury.

The 31-year-old striker pulled up on the halfway line in the early stages of his side's 1-0 home league win over Motherwell and walked straight up the tunnel when being replaced by eventual matchwinner Ryan Naderi in the eighth minute.

McInnes did hand £9million new boy Kevin Kelsy a late cameo appearance and will no doubt ask more from him moving forward with Youssef Chermiti also out for the season, but his thoughts last night were focused on his skipper’s welfare ahead of a scan.

Shankland missed more than two months of action at the turn of the year when working under McInnes at Hearts – with this latest setback also ruling him out of new Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli’s plans for the Nations League double-header with Slovenia and Switzerland later this month.

‘He has a similar feeling to the hamstring injury he had at Hearts last January when he was out for three months,’ said McInnes. ‘Obviously, we don’t want to speculate too much, but he says it feels similar and in the same area.

‘We’ll get him scanned on Monday. His output was really high on Wednesday at Falkirk on the 4G (pitch). Sometimes, going from pitch to pitch, different surfaces, can maybe make you a wee bit more vulnerable.

Lawrence Shankland faces a period on the sidelines after picking up a hamstring injury

‘He says he felt fine going into the game and there was nothing really that he did in the game that he was aware of. He just felt it and pulled up.

'It’s a shame for the boy because he was obviously in good form, getting himself moving and enjoying some of that attacking threat we’ve had over the last few games.

‘We’ve waited long and hard for that, so it is just a pity for Lawrence that it looks as if, in the next period, he’s going to be sitting on the sidelines.

‘If somebody had said to me walking in the door that Chermiti and Shankland were going to be injured with significant injuries, you know, you’d have felt the weight of that.

‘Getting Kevin was such a good bit of business and the club deserve a lot of credit for that. I thought he came on and got to the pitch of the game really well. He’s such a good mover, strong boy.

‘There was obviously a temptation to bring him on after five minutes, but, and much to the crowd’s disappointment, I had a conversation with Kevin yesterday.

'He said he felt a bit stiff and tight from the previous couple of days training and the fact that he travelled.

Shankland passes the captain's armband on to midfielder Dan Neil as he leaves the picth

‘If it’s not the right decision to start him, it’s probably the right decision not to bring him on after five minutes and put the No 9 position maybe more at risk.

‘I was delighted for Ryan too. The good thing with Ryan is, even when he’s not at his best, he puts himself about.

'He lets centre-halves know he’s there. He presses brilliantly.

‘He gets his goal, he gets a bit of confidence for that, and he probably could have added to the one goal he got, but it was a strong performance from him. We’re going to need that squad to call upon.

‘Bojan Miovski wasn’t in the squad, but we’ve still got a guy who knows his way about the Scottish Premier League and can score.

‘Having Ryan, Kevin, Bojan and Min-su Kim, who can play central, we’ve still got some decent options there.’

McInnes also reported himself happy with the nature of yesterday’s victory over Motherwell, his side’s third straight league win.

Rangers manager Derek McInnes watches from the stand as he served his touchline ban

‘I thought the scoreline made it suggest it was tighter than it actually was,’ he said. ‘Motherwell are good enough to create opportunities, but I thought we nullified their threat throughout the game, really, other than maybe one or two moments on transitions.

‘In terms of chances created, penalty-box entries, big chances missed? You know, we’re just disappointed we’ve not added to the one goal, but one was enough today. It might not be in future, so we’ve got to make sure we get those improvements and put teams to bed.’

McInnes also felt vice-captain Dan Neil delivered a display to silence some of his early doubters.

‘I thought Dan was strong. I’m delighted that everybody’s recognising that. I think it’s probably his best performance since he came to the club,’ he reported.

‘What I enjoyed even from my vantage point today was I could hear Dan and Nico (Raskin) speaking, organising, and really driving the press, and I thought we turned the ball over so many times.’

Meanwhile, Motherwell head coach Alfred Johansson chose to praise keeper Alex Paulsen for some of his saves over the 90 minutes despite the fact he was caught in possession at the edge of his own box for the Naderi goal that secured the points.

Motherwell goalkeeper Alex Paulsen can only watch as his error gifts Ryan Naderi a tap-in

‘You don’t want to concede goals. It doesn’t matter if it’s this or that,’ he said. ‘The reason why it stays 1-0 today is also because of Alex Paulsen.

‘With how consistent he’s been, how many clean sheets we’ve been having this last season, it’s not even a point.

‘Congratulations to Rangers, I think they were better than us. We didn’t play to our best, especially not on the ball. Then the game becomes too much transitions, and Rangers are good there.

‘I think, in the second half, we tried to go for it a little bit more, but, over the 90 minutes, I think we were not good enough.’

Sports.title: Spurs goalless start to the season raises questions over Richarlison's exile as hosts fume over disallowed goal: Nottingham Forest 0-0 Tottenham
Sports.content:
Spurs goalless start to the season raises questions over Richarlison's exile as hosts fume over disallowed goal: Nottingham Forest 0-0 Tottenham

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

No goals in three games leaves Tottenham to ponder the wisdom of exiling last season’s top scorer while Nottingham Forest were left to seethe over the goal that was ruled out.

It was bundled into the net by Neco Williams in the second half, seemed briefly set to become the difference between these two imperfect teams and would fuel the post-match debate.

James McAtee was the architect with a pass to release Morgan Gibbs-White, whose shot clipped goalkeeper Toni Kinsky and spun onwards towards the open goal.

Sandro Tonali, chasing back, missed the ball with his first attempt to clear and Williams arrived with momentum behind him and threw himself forward as the £100million Spurs midfielder prepared another clearance.

By this time, Tonali was back on his own goal line, off balance and struggling. Williams smothered him and Forest ran off to celebrate. Only when the slow-motion replays were scrutinised was it evident that the ball had struck Williams on a hand from point blank range.

Referee Craig Pawson took advice from his VAR and disallowed the goal, which incensed the home crowd and ensured a humdrum contest ended with the result it probably deserved.

Neco Williams saw a scrappy goal chalked off for handball to ensure Nottingham Forest and Tottenham finished goalless

Craig Pawson's took advice from his VAR and disallowed the goal, incensing the hosts

Roberto De Zerbi's side earned their first point of the campaign but a growing focus is on where Tottenham's goals are going to come from

For Roberto De Zerbi, a first point of the season is progress of sorts. There were signs of improvement for him to cling to, but after a week in which Spurs missed transfer targets and exiled Richarlison, all eyes were on where goals were going to come from.

In short, they didn’t. The visitors had a dozen efforts at goal without registering any on target.

Spurs have sold or discarded their top scorer in each of the last four seasons, starting with Harry Kane and Heung-min Son and Brennan Johnson, who was sold in January.

In the search for someone to shoulder this burden, eyes turned instinctively to Omar Marmoush, selected to lead the line albeit not in the traditional sense.

Marmoush is not going to hold the ball up with his back to goal and link play, but his movement is slick and there were flickers of promise.

One when he burst onto a pass by Pedro Porro before firing wide in the first half.

Whistle-happy referee Pawson called it back for a foul on Williams, a generous decision. Even so, perhaps the Egyptian on loan from Manchester City would’ve felt happier if he found the net.

Another chance on the break in the second half from a long punt by Kinsky was blazed over by Marmoush from a good position. De Zerbi took issue here with Marmoush’s decision to go for goal when there were passing options.

There were flickers of promise from Omar Marmoush but Tottenham are still yet to score three matches into the season

Dominic Solanke, who replaced him near the end, headed over the last of the Spurs chances, from a cross by Mohamed Kudus.

True to his style, Oliver Glasner’s Forest were comfortable conceding plenty of possession, direct and were dangerous on the turnover and had the better openings of the first half.

Liam Delap released Gibbs-White two minutes before the interval. Kinsky raced out to make a strong save. There was a flag up, but it looked onside. Murillo, Jair Cunha and Delap all fizzed efforts over in the first half.

Delap was making his first start for Forest after his £50million move from Chelsea. Spurs required no introduction to his combative style. On his last appearance against them, he broke Djed Spence’s jaw with a forearm slam.

Forest opened with a long ball from keeper Mats Sels for Delap to contest in the air. Brentford dominated De Zerbi’s team on the opening day but here they offered more resistance.

Much better defensively, and far more aggressive and competitive in midfield where Tonali and Rodrigo Bentancur were effective, off the ball more than on it.

Spurs could not penetrate Forest’s well drilled defence, with three central defenders and hard-working wing backs ready to reinforce in a defensive five.

Savio, one of three changes to the team beaten at home by Newcastle skipped past one or two challenges early in the game, but the red shirts often crowded him out.

Mykhailo Mudryk came on for his Tottenham debut and his first appearance for 646 days

Spurs made a positive start to the second half, generating a good period of pressure and threatening to create more with Mathys Tel, Conor Gallagher and Savio on the ball in more advanced areas.

Still, Forest held firm, helped by the finishing.

Marmoush smashed a free kick into a wall and Micky van de Ven headed wide at the near post from a corner. Having got the better of goalkeeper Sels without conceding a foul and at such close range, it was a chance Van de Ven ought to have scored.

Glasner sent on Daniel Munoz for a debut and Igor Jesus and Forest regained control.

The goal was controversially ruled out, and home fans were still fuming when Pawson ignored claims for a penalty from Jesus, convinced he had been fouled by Bentancur as he tried to get on the end of a cross.

Glasner also thought his team deserved a penalty for a foul by Kudus, a nudge on Williams under a high ball.

Mykhailo Mudryk came on for a debut and his first appearance for 646 days, but this was destined to remain goalless, and the first time since 1974 Spurs have failed to score in their opening three league games.

Sports.title: Serena and Venus Williams avoid $100,000 in fines after skipping media duties after US Open doubles defeat
Sports.content:
Serena and Venus Williams swerved fines totalling $100,000 (£82,925) after skipping media duties in the wake of their first-round doubles defeat at this year’s US Open.

The superstar siblings were obligated to speak to the press after their three-hour battle against Maya Joint and Chan Hao-ching and might have each incurred a fine of up to $50,000, as per Grand Slam rules, unless deemed unable to appear on ‘reasonable grounds’ such as illness or injury.

The US Open confirmed however that neither player will receive a fine.

In the aftermath of their defeat, on Saturday, Serena simply posted pictures of herself walking onto court with her sister, captioning the post with the symbol for infinity to represent their strong bond.

Serena appeared to have snubbed the pressroom at Wimbledon in July after defeat to Joint in the singles as a wildcard but later shared that she had ‘tweaked’ her knee - an issue which forced her out of a second doubles debut with Venus in SW19.

Then, Williams shared that she had been doing 'everything' to ensure she could return to court, posting a statement on social media before she was forced to withdraw.

Venus and Serena Williams have avoided receiving fines of $50,000 apiece after they snubbed the press room after their US Open doubles match

The sisters were dumped out of the US Open women's doubles in round one on Friday

'It felt so good to be back on the grass at Wimbledon,' Williams wrote on Instagram. 'I’m incredibly thankful for the wild card - and even more grateful my daughters got to see that it’s never too late to chase something you love.

'I tweaked my knee late in the first set, but I’ll be doing everything I can to be ready for doubles with Venus. Congratulations to Maya Joint on a great match, and thank you to everyone who showed up and showed me so much love. That feeling will never get old.'

Some tennis fans took offense with the sisters' media snub, suggesting it was unprofessional behavior from the legends.

'So rude of them. US Open puts them on Ashe primetime, gives Venus a wildcard to play singles and this is how they act. #noclass,' one social media user wrote.

'Both of them should show some class…..they are looked up to as role models (for some reason)….these are poor examples to set for younger people,' said another.

'So disrespectful. 0 class. And not the first time. Stop giving them wild cards,' posted one fan.

ESPN broadcaster and former tennis star Patrick McEnroe wrote: 'Incredible vibe last match @usopen calling the Williams sisters doubles match.

'ONLY THEY COULD fill the stadium for a doubles match. SHOW UP FOR THE POST MATCH PRESS CONFERENCE.'

Serena and her sister were partnering at the US Open for the first time in four years on Friday

But they could not get the better of Australia's Maya Joint (left) and Taiwan's Chan Hao-ching

However, other sympathetic fans defended the Williams sisters with one posting: 'These women don't owe anyone anything, especially at this stage in their careers...to all the disgusting so called tennis fans in these comments.'

'Please take several seats. It's always going to be something you don't like about them. They are legends and can do as they please,' added another.

'There's nothing you could possibly ask that we need to know. They all should start skipping. Get rid of on court interviews too. Dumb a** questions about nothing,' a third echoed.

'The thing is you're kind of hyenas, I can't blame them,' said a fourth.

Earlier this week, Venus spoke to the press after her first-round singles exit to Sofia Kenin.

The living legends were handed their third doubles wildcard of the summer in Flushing Meadows, with 23-time Grand Slam champion Serena also featuring in the mixed event alongside Carlos Alcaraz, losing in the quarter-finals to finalists Flavio Cobolli and Belinda Bencic.

Between them, Serena and Venus have won 14 Grand Slam doubles titles and three Olympic gold medals, but were unable to see victory across the line after pushing Chan and Joint to three tough sets spanning over three hours.

The younger pair had envisaged getting over the line in straight sets before the experienced sibling duo forced a tiebreak and raised their level when it counted.

Despite doing the same in the third set, and building a 5-0 lead however, errors which had been creeping into their game in the opening set saw them falter at the last minute, with Chan and Joint carrying off the win 6-3, 6-7(6), 7-6(7).

Sports.title: Cardiff's former Arsenal star Krystian Bielik grabs young fan by the throat - before being slapped back - and gets away without any punishment in bizarre incident
Sports.content:
Cardiff's Krystian Bielik appeared to grab a supporter by the throat during a bizarre confrontation during their Championship match against Portsmouth.

The incident occurred in the 70th minute at Fratton Park, with Cardiff trailing 2-0 to the hosts.

Bielik, a former Arsenal youth product, had attempted to gather the ball from the stands.

Footage showed a young fan throwing the ball away from the Cardiff midfielder.

The act prompted a reaction from Bielik, who could be seen reaching out towards the fan's throat and pushing them away.

The fan responded by standing up and appearing to try to push Bielik in retaliation.

So Bielek grabs a kids throat, kid defends himself, and kid gets thrown out. Portsmouth FC should give off about this and Bielek needs suspending! pic.twitter.com/9Np1k8Xl3i — Charlie Barnes (@ChaltJames) September 5, 2026

Cardiff's Krystian Bielik appeared to grab the throat of a young Portsmouth fan after they threw the ball away from him

Another supporter could also be seen throwing the ball at Bielik in the aftermath but struck his Cardiff team-mate Perry Ng.

Following a delay, the supporter involved in the initial incident was ejected from the stadium for their part in the incident while Bielik avoided punishment.

Both Portsmouth manager John Mousinho and his Cardiff counterpart Brian Barry-Murphy were spoken to by the referee, as well as captains from both teams.

Portsmouth would ultimately go on to secure a 2-0 victory over their newly promoted opponents.

Bielik, 28, was making just his fourth appearance for Cardiff after joining the Bluebirds last month.

Barry-Murphy claimed post-match that Bielik 'got slapped in the face' by the fan and praised the referee's handling of the incident.

'I wanted to make sure he (Bielik) was protected and make sure he was okay, which he is.

'I thought the referee and his staff handled the incident impeccably.

'He said he'd seen everything which occurred really clearly, so he diffused the situation and implemented the correct processes from there.

'The players are always subjected to different things that's not acceptable.

'My job is to protect the players, but really I'm trying to make sure that we play well and win.

'I'm sure the FA will look at it and implement the correct processes.'

The fan was ejected from the stadium following the incident, while Bielik avoided punishment

Portsmouth boss Mousinho offered an apology to Cardiff and their players following the incident.

'The referee said that, as Krystian went to get the ball, there was a little bit of a kerfuffle and one of the supporters struck him.

'It wasn't a good incident. I have just seen him there, and he was OK, but that's not the point, we can't be having that.

'We want to create a really difficult atmosphere at Fratton Park, we have done that successfully over the past few years.

'Sometimes it tips over, I understand that, I don't think it needs to tip over to that extent.

'We extend our apologies to the players, Cardiff and make sure we can try to cut it out.'

Sports.title: Man City 1-0 Coventry: New £125m man Enzo Fernandez takes first step towards paying off his price tag, Rayan Cherki strengthens his claim to be Enzo Maresca's key creative spark - and the flaws the narrow win exposed
Sports.content:
Man City 1-0 Coventry: New £125m man Enzo Fernandez takes first step towards paying off his price tag, Rayan Cherki strengthens his claim to be Enzo Maresca's key creative spark - and the flaws the narrow win exposed

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A late call, a great ball, and one small step towards paying off the most baffling transfer fee of the window. Those hoping for Enzo Fernandez to fall flat at Manchester City will have to wait a while longer to land their punches.

We can state at the outset that the Argentine did not settle this game – that was achieved by the more conventional means of Erling Haaland.

Nor was Fernandez the best player, because Rayan Cherki seems to hold a standing reservation on that status.

But in a game that lacked any sustained periods of class from City, Fernandez, the £125million riddle, bedded himself in with a solid contribution and one sublime delivery.

Relevantly, it was the ball that orchestrated the winning moment after 26 minutes, when he spotted the run of Antoine Semenyo, processed the space behind Jay Dasilva, and through a split-second judgement was able to shape the two factors into a high-quality, game-changing pass.

From there, Semenyo nailed the cross and Haaland did what Haaland does, but the art had been supplied by a man who most neutrals prefer to despise. Presumably, he won’t wait too long to offer a reminder of the infuriating aspects he showed at Chelsea, and at the World Cup, but this was a strong start.

Erling Haaland celebrates scoring the only goal of the game for Man City against Coventry

Enzo Fernandez was listed among Enzo Maresca’s substitutes, only to be promoted to the XI when Nico O’Reilly tweaked his back

And a strange one, too, given Fernandez was listed among Enzo Maresca’s substitutes, only to be promoted to the XI when Nico O’Reilly tweaked his back in the warm-up.

In truth, that setback wasn’t the only hurdle Maresca faced. Sure, this was City’s third win in three, but it was also messy, wasteful, and far closer than anyone expected. Coventry had good chances in both halves from only 22 per cent of the possession.

Credit there to Frank Lampard – each of his substitutions after the break enhanced Coventry’s side, which might have been worth something had Gianluigi Donnarumma not made a string of saves, but it is hard to escape their record. At three defeats from three, they are the mirror to City in every way.

Maresca, therefore, won’t read volumes into this beyond the result, but can share the broader excitement whenever Cherki takes possession. He neither scored nor assisted here, but with two of each preceding another menacing contribution, his confidence is glowing in fluorescent shades, especially when he is permitted to play that advanced role behind Haaland.

To that end, Fernandez’s arrival in deeper areas ought to help.
