World.title: Romania Opens New Human Trafficking Case Against Tate Brothers
World.content:
Andrew and Tristan Tate arrive at court for a pre-trial hearing in Bucharest, February 2024. Photo: EPA-EFE/Robert Ghement.

Romanian anti-organised crime prosecutors on Thursday evening indicted British-American influencers Andrew and Tristan Tate in a new case involving alleged trafficking of minors, according to court records seen by BIRN.

Prosecutors accuse the defendants, together with two Romanian nationals, of trafficking minors and related offences, including money laundering.

The new indictment follows a December 2024 decision by the Bucharest Court of Appeal to return the original case file to prosecutors for the investigation to be redone.

Romania’s anti-organised crime agency, DIICOT, subsequently expanded its investigation and brought additional charges.

According to judicial sources cited by online publication HotNews, some of the allegations have been separated from the broader investigation in order to avoid the risk of statutory limitation.

The brothers have been under investigation in Romania since their initial arrest in December 2022.

They face various allegations, including human trafficking, rape, trafficking of minors, sexual intercourse with a minor and money-laundering.

In June, prosecutors expanded their investigation into Andrew Tate to cover new allegations that he sexually exploited a woman in 2017, taking advantage of her vulnerable situation to induce her to produce sexually explicit content and perform video chat activities – and that he and his brother, Tristan, laundered almost 3 million euros earned from human trafficking via two companies between 2018 and 2022.

The Tate brothers have denied wrongdoing.

Despite being arrested in 2022, the case against them has made slow progress: in late 2024, a court returned the original indictment to prosecutors, saying it was flawed, and in February 2025 DIICOT permitted the brothers to leave Romania, despite the ongoing case.

They are currently in the United States, contesting extradition to the United Kingdom, where authorities have brought nearly 60 charges against them, including rape, human trafficking and sexual exploitation.

Both brothers have described the cases against them as politically motivated and unfounded.

World.title: Democracy Digest: Poland Investigates Arson of Drone Factory as Suspected Russian Sabotage
World.content:
Hungary PM looks to recover ECJ fines; Orban’s son central figure in Chad mission

Statements made by PM Peter Magyar this week indicate that Hungary might not be the kind of pliant partner the EU had hoped for after his predecessor, Viktor Orban, was turfed out of office. Magyar met with Manfred Weber, leader of the European People’s Party (EPP), and European Council President Antonio Costa earlier this week, and made clear he would strongly defend Hungary’s rights and interests during the talks over the next seven-year EU budget (MFF). Magyar said in a Facebook post that his Tisza party would like to become a full member of the EPP, the European political family of centre-right parties that Orban’s Fidesz left in 2021 before being expelled. However, before that can happen, the Article 7 procedure – a punitive measure which removes voting rights of member states – against Hungary would have to be closed, he said. The procedure was launched by the European Parliament in 2018, but needs a formal decision by the Council of the EU to end the process. Magyar also touched on the sensitive subject of the 1 million euros that Hungary is paying daily for failing to comply with EU asylum regulations. The case dates back to the Orban government’s decision to close the controversial transit zones at the border, while making it next-to-impossible to submit asylum applications from inside Hungary. Under the current system, asylum applications can only be submitted at Hungarian embassies in Belgrade or Kyiv. Last year, Hungary received 113 asylum applications and granted refugee status, subsidiary or humanitarian protection to just 35 people. Weber reportedly offered to help in settling the issue, but Magyar stressed the border fence will have to remain in place. Reopening the transit zones would be highly controversial, as the opposition would use it as evidence Magyar is bowing to pressure from Brussels. On the other hand, the fines have already reached around 1 billion euros – a significant loss of revenue for the Hungarian budget. Magyar floated the idea of recovering this money in the framework of the MFF negotiations. In another move likely to be frowned on in Brussels, the Hungarian government blocked Ukraine’s EU accession process for the third time this week, arguing insufficient progress on minority rights.

The family of former PM Orban was back in the headlines this week as documents obtained by news site 444.hu confirmed what had long been suspected – that Orban’s son, Gaspar, was the driving force behind Hungary’s planned military mission to Chad (and not the wild conspiracy theory of Hungary serving Russian interests in the region). The idea originated during a trip to Niger in May 2023 by Orban Jnr and Tristan Azbej, Hungary’s deputy state secretary responsible for helping persecuted Christians. The two initially planned an agricultural project there – a model camel farm supported by the Hungarian University of Agriculture and Life Sciences. Farmers from Niger would have been instructed by Hungarian experts on how to process camel milk and produce dairy products. However, after a military coup in Niger in 2023 attention shifted to Chad, where the project’s aims were significantly expanded. In addition to the planned model farm, it was to include a medical and a military mission involving up to 200 Hungarian soldiers. According to the documents now obtained, Orban Jnr functioned as the pro-forma leader and central coordinator of the project. Virtually all major decisions – from when to buy plane tickets for experts to arranging the shipment of medical equipment – depended on him. In a previous interview, former defence minister Kristof Szalay-Bobrovniczky had tried to defend the mission and Orban Jnr’s role in it: “Gaspar Orban is a military officer… He goes wherever he is ordered to go. I assigned him as a liaison officer.” The newly published documents prove otherwise. In the end, the Chad government lost enthusiasm for the project. Although 27 billion forints (73.5 million euros) were earmarked for the mission in the 2026 budget, the plan was quietly shelved by Orban as the April election approached.

World.title: HNS Confirms: Luka Modrić Continues With National Team
World.content:
Croatia national team captain Luka Modrić will be on the squad list that head coach Slaven Bilić announces on Monday for the Nations League fixtures against Czechia, Spain and England.

Modrić has confirmed to Bilić and Croatian Football Federation (HNS) president Marijan Kustić that he remains available for the national team in the new edition of the Nations League. The legendary international career of a player who has left an indelible mark across 202 caps for Croatia and led the country to its greatest successes will thus continue.

“Of course I’m delighted by Luka’s decision, because we all know what he represents and means for Croatia, both on and off the pitch. I’m especially pleased that after 14 years we’ll be working together again, sharing the strong ambition for Croatia to be strong, successful and on a par with the best in the world,” said head coach Slaven Bilić.

The head coach will unveil the squad list on Monday ahead of the September gathering for matches against Czechia (26 September, in Prague), Spain (29 September, in Seville), England (3 October, in Rijeka) and Spain again (6 October, in Split).

World.title: Dubrovnik Getting New Transatlantic Route: From May 2027 Direct to Montreal
World.content:
September the 5th, 2026 – Dubrovnik is set to get a new transatlantic route from May 2027, linking the Pearl of the Adriatic with Montreal directly.

Dubrovnik will be directly connected to Montreal from May 2027. Canada’s largest airline, Air Canada, is introducing a seasonal route between the two cities, with the first flight announced for 11 May 2027. As reported by DuList, the new route is part of Air Canada’s expansion for the 2027 summer season, during which the company is also introducing several other new international destinations, including Oslo, Basel, Shannon and Guangzhou.

For Dubrovnik specifically, this is an important step in strengthening direct connectivity with the North American market. Montreal is one of Air Canada’s more significant hubs, so the new route will also open up onward travel options for passengers from Dubrovnik to other Canadian and American cities.

According to data from Air Canada’s sales system, tickets for the new route have already appeared on sale. A return economy-class ticket for travel from 12 to 26 June 2027 is currently selling, for example, for around 1,256 Canadian dollars. Prices can of course change depending on the travel dates and availability. Air Canada has previously operated services to Croatia, and this time the choice has fallen on Dubrovnik. The new route could additionally contribute to attracting Canadian visitors and to extending the tourist season, given that operations begin as early as mid-May. A detailed flight schedule, including the exact number of weekly rotations and the end of seasonal operations, has not yet been published.

World.title: Secrets of Cape Škamica – Forgotten Sundial From Southern Pag Saved
World.content:
September the 5th, 2026 – Cape Škamica is a very isolated point, and a long-forgotten sundial from this southern part of the island of Pag has been saved.

On the solitary Cape Škamica on the southern part of the island of Pag, an unusual stone monument – a historic sundial – has been saved from decay. Ana Zunic reports for Morski that following years of exposure to the harsh bura wind, salt and the blows of the jugo, the object that bears witness to past times has been successfully reconstructed. Despite the restoration, it still keeps its greatest secret to itself, and that is that no one knows with certainty who built it and exactly when.

Archaeological research in Zadar and Split has so far offered no concrete written traces or plans. Local tradition attributes the construction to Jure Komadina from Vlašići, citing the similarity of the building technique with a nearby village well, while another theory places the origin of the structure in the era of the Austro-Hungarian monarchy.

fishermen and shepherds knew it well

Although historical documents are lacking, testimonies of older locals confirm that the sundial truly served its purpose. Roman numerals were once carved into it and an iron pin was fitted that cast a shadow to indicate the time. Located on an important maritime corridor – with a view of the Pag Bridge, Velebit and the islets of Mali and Veliki Sikavac, the sundial served for centuries as a key landmark for shepherds from Vlašići and Smokvica and fishermen from Vrsi. Before the recent intervention the structure was in extremely poor condition, without binding material and with significantly damaged plaster. The comprehensive restoration was financially supported by the City of Pag and the Municipality of Vrsi, with the involvement of the association “Volim Vlašići”, experts Šime Stojak and Šime Glavan, and the contractor Travej d.o.o. The archaeological survey and documentation were prepared by archaeologists Neda and Igor Kulenović, under the conservator supervision of Ivan Matković.

both roman and arabic numerals are on the sundial

During the reconstruction the damaged stone blocks were replaced, and both Roman numerals (for winter time reckoning) and Arabic numerals (for summer time reckoning) were precisely carved into the new plaster, along with half-hour markings. The entire construction was finally protected with a special impregnation. The initiative launched back in 2020 has thus finally reached its conclusion, but the work is not finished. Although the monument has been saved, it still does not have formal status as a cultural asset, which is why the initiators will submit a proposal to the City of Pag for its protection and entry into the Register of Cultural Assets of the Republic of Croatia.

The site has already become part of the Pag Outdoor tourist offer; an approximately four-kilometre-long hiking trail leads to it from the direction of Vlašići and Smokvica. Plans also include the installation of an information board that will acquaint visitors with the history, restoration and the mystery that still surrounds this stone monument on Cape Škamica.

World.title: Men Removed From Croatia After Glorifying Ratko Mladić in Dubrovnik
World.content:
September the 5th, 2026 – Several men, some of whom are citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina, have been removed from Croatia after glorifying war criminal Ratko Mladić in the Dubrovnik area.

Police officers working for the Dubrovnik-Neretva Police Administration have now conducted criminal investigations that ran from the 28th of August to the 2nd of September 2026. Morski reports that those investigations were launched against four citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina who were temporarily in Croatia (aged 31, 30, 25 and 25) and against one 35-year-old Croatian citizen.

All of the men were arrested for publishing content which glorified and supported Ratko Mladić. The police conducted the criminal investigations after receiving several reports from members of the public. It was established that the men, on publicly accessible social media profiles, had published pictures, symbols, songs and texts with which they paid tribute to and expressed gratitude to Mladić.

expulsion from croatia for the non-citizens

Three of the men who are citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina have already been brought before the Municipal Court in Dubrovnik, where they were non-finally found guilty and issued with monetary fines. After that, their residence and work permits will be revoked and their short-term stay in Croatia terminated, with a three-month ban on entry into the country.

Proceedings for expulsion from the European Economic Area with a two-year entry ban have also been initiated against them; the ban will take effect after the judgement becomes final. The fourth foreign national, as well as the Croatian citizen, will also be brought before the Municipal Court in Dubrovnik.

World.title: One of the Most Important Lowland Fortresses in Croatia Is Being Restored
World.content:
September the 5th, 2026 – One of the most significant lowland fortresses in all of Croatia is currently being restored, with two lakes also set to be arranged alongside it.

There are few historical fortresses and castles for which most people’s first association is an animal, but that is exactly the case with Đurđevac. The Old Town of Đurđevac is inseparably connected with the rooster, and the famous legend of the Picoki has marked its identity. Lana Mindoljevic writes for Putni kofer however that this fortress is much more than that legend, and a thorough restoration is currently underway that will restore its former glory and bring a series of new contents.

a rare example of a preserved fortress between the drava and the sava

OLYMPUS DIGITAL CAMERA

This defensive bastion protected the town from enemies for centuries, and today it is a meeting place and one of the most important galleries in northern Croatia. It does not impress with its size, but with the stories it hides. Its walls tell of sieges, the legendary rooster, and also of a gallery thanks to which this castle could easily find itself on the cultural map of much larger European cities. The Old Town of Đurđevac was built at the end of the 15th century, at a time when Ottoman threats were an everyday reality. Situated on a sandy elevation and surrounded by marshes, it was strategically conceived as a defensive point in the lowland part of Podravina. Today it is one of the rare preserved lowland fortresses between the Sava and the Drava, and precisely this context gives it additional weight. It was never a nobleman’s castle, but a fortress of the community.

a realistic restoration process

As the City of Đurđevac announced on its Facebook page, the reconstruction of the ramparts of the Old Town is restoring the fortress’s recognisable appearance. Works are in progress, and intensive work is currently under way on the construction of the rampart tower, which will soon be fully completed. The restoration of the ramparts is, they write, an important step in restoring the historical vista of the Old Town, but also in creating new contents that will further enrich the city’s tourist offer. More than 1.3 million euros has been secured for the revitalisation of the complex. “The restored ramparts will also receive a new tourist function. As part of the project, the arrangement of a Podravinoteka with an offer of products from local producers is planned, while through the Green Infrastructure project the surroundings of the fortress will also be arranged. The area around the Old Town will be enriched with new walking paths, lighting, a stage and auditorium, as well as two lakes that will further emphasise the historical and landscape value of this space,” state the City’s representatives on the Facebook page.

the story of a rooster that sent the ottomans packing

We mentioned at the beginning that the identity of the fortress is inseparably linked to the legend of the Picoki, which perfectly illustrates the importance it had for the community. You can read the full (and extremely heartwarming) story here.

The Old Town of Đurđevac itself was built simply, but very thoughtfully. It has a recognisable polygonal ground plan with an inner courtyard and a strong defensive tower that dominates the space. Although it was extended and adapted over the centuries, it has preserved its original defensive appearance and character. Unlike many historical fortresses that have remained merely a backdrop of the past, the Old Town of Đurđevac today has an exceptionally lively cultural function. The Museum of the City of Đurđevac operates in it, as does an interpretation centre dedicated to the Picokijada, and gallery spaces that attract visitors from all over Croatia. In recent years, works by Pablo Picasso, Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec, Salvador Dalí and Joan Miró have been exhibited here! Of course, these are their lesser-known works, but that did not bother the thousands of people who visited the exhibitions in the slightest.

the home of some of the most important croatian works of art

The attic of the fortress also hides a true artistic treasure. “A turning point in the museum, cultural and tourist sense was contributed by the Donation of the Croatian painter Ivan Lacković Croata, with more than 2,000 museological units, works from the art collection of Croatian authors and authors from numerous countries of the world,” it is stated on the website of the Tourist Board of Đurđevac. Visitors can see works by Vlaho Bukovac, Bela Čikoš Sesija, Menci Clement Crnčić, Ljubo Babić and many others here. Precisely this concentration of top artistic names makes Đurđevac an unexpected but extremely valuable cultural destination.

Croata’s donation today forms the permanent exhibition of the Museum of the City of Đurđevac; it is located in the authentic attic of the fortress and numbers 163 masterpieces of Croatian artists from the end of the 19th and the 20th century, from paintings and graphics to sculptures and posters. “It is one of the most valuable artistic donations in Croatia, and the collection itself is often described as a ‘small Croatian Louvre,’” states the Tourist Board of Đurđevac.

Đurđevac is a quiet and gentle Podravina town that, together with its surroundings, has a little fewer than 7,500 inhabitants. Yet this small place hides an incredible history and attractions that you will not find anywhere else in Croatia! The best-known is, of course, the “Croatian Sahara.” True, its size, compared with the African original, is like a grain of sand. But the modest size does not diminish its special character. The Đurđevac Sands are a unique reserve, and right next to the Old Town of Đurđevac a zoo called Croatian Sahara has been arranged where you can see real camels, as well as goats, sheep, horses, llamas and more. This is a fairly unusual place, without a doubt one of the most unusual attractions of continental Croatia. Đurđevac is not a place you will just rush through. Get to know it at leisure, surrender to its stories, and if you want to experience a real celebration, head to the town in June and take part in the legendary Picokijada.

World.title: Croatia Set to Purchase Powerful Korean Rocket System
World.content:
September the 4th, 2026 – Croatia is set to purchase a powerful Korean rocket system, with the first talks between the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Croatia (MORH) and the South Korean Ministry of Defence on military cooperation actually having begun a year ago.

The government will adopt a decision on the purchase of 18 self-propelled multiple rocket launchers Chunmoo K239, with the accompanying rockets, for 435.2 million euros excluding VAT. As Krešimir Žabec learns for Jutarnji list, with this system Croatia will obtain rockets with a range from 30 to more than 300 kilometres, including ballistic missiles for deterrence.

procurement details

It’s currently expected that Defence Minister Ivan Anušić will soon sign a contract with the South Korean company Hanwha Aerospace. Cooperation will also be contracted with the Polish company WB Group, which will install the command-and-control system (C2). Poslovni reports that according to available information, 85 percent of the contracted system will be delivered by 2028. Payment is planned in the period from 2026 to 2029. As touched on above, the first talks between MORH and the South Korean Ministry of Defence on military cooperation actually began a year ago. Back at the end of 2024, Croatia contracted the purchase of eight HIMARS systems with the United States, but the US, due to the needs of its own army, suspended the delivery of 300-kilometre-range rockets to allies, while a sales ban applies to those with a range of 500 kilometres.

Because of this, Croatia opted for a solution that has already been chosen by Poland, Norway and Estonia. Compared with HIMARS, Chunmoo also offers twice the firepower because it has two rocket containers with a total of 12 rockets, while HIMARS has one with six. Support for the purchase was also given by Prime Minister Andrej Plenković and President Zoran Milanović. Two months ago in Ankara, after the NATO summit, Milanović announced the acquisition of new armaments as a response to Serbia’s purchase of the Israeli PULS system. “We will have to counter that as a state in some way, by equipping ourselves with something similar,” he said at the time.

training and the technical parts

The Chunmoo K239 system consists of a mobile launcher on a truck, a fire-control system and a communication system. Its key advantage is the possibility of using different types of rockets from standardised modular containers. It is the only operational system of this type that can simultaneously use rockets of different calibres on the same launcher.

The commander in the field can thus at any moment fire a rocket adapted to the mission, without the need for modifications. For example, four 280 mm rockets can be placed in one container, and six guided 239 mm rockets in the other. If the most powerful ballistic missile CTM-290 of 600 mm calibre, with a range greater than 300 kilometres, is used, one such projectile is placed in one container. Its trajectory after launch reaches an altitude of between 25 and 40 kilometres before diving towards the target.

The rate of fire depends on the calibre. The system can fire 12 guided 239 mm rockets in less than a minute. The entire system is operated by a three-member crew. The contract covers the launchers and rockets, logistical support and training lasting six weeks. 100 soldiers will be needed to operate all 18 launchers. The largest part of the system will be delivered in 2028, and at this moment it is a secret where it will be stationed within the ranks of the Croatian Army.

World.title: Varaždin to Ban Sale of Alcohol in Shops After 22:00
World.content:
September the 4th, 2026 – The continental Croatian city of Varaždin is set to become to first continental city to introduce a ban on the sale of alcohol in shops and kiosks after 22:00.

Varaždin will become the first continental city in Croatia to introduce a ban on the sale of alcohol in shops and at petrol stations after 22:00, but that isn’t the only ban. Net.hr reports that those who are caught consuming alcohol in public areas outside of the premises of bars, restaurants and cafes could also face penalties, regardless of when they purchased it.

Varaždin residents will no longer be able to get hold of alcohol so easily in the evening hours. Just as some coastal cities have already done earlier, Varaždin is introducing this new measure. “For the reason that our fellow citizens requested it. Constant disturbance of public order and peace, especially around petrol stations, particularly the one in Zrinski and Frankopan Street, daily complaints from people who nevertheless deserve to have peace and a night’s rest – these are the main reasons,” said Neven Bosilj, Mayor of Varaždin. In shops and at petrol stations, the sale of alcohol will not be allowed from 22:00 until 07:00.

the consumption of alcohol in public will also be banned

Drinking alcohol out in public anywhere outside of the premises of bars, cafes and restaurants will also be subject to a ban. Anyone caught by the police and municipal wardens will have to pay a fine of up to 260 euros for the offence. In the night-time hours, alcohol will still be able to be consumed legally only in restaurants, bars and cafes. Many owners of such establishments can now expect higher turnover because of the move.

Whether people are complying with the new rules will be controlled by the police and municipal wardens, of whom there are not enough, so the mayor has announced the following:

“We’re announcing a tender for new municipal wardens because the state has also transferred various powers, since they cannot find people for construction inspections, so they transfer certain jobs to units of local self-government. That’s why we’re strengthening it,” said Mayor Bosilj. After the public consultation is completed, the decision on the restricted sale will be voted on by the City Council, and it is expected to enter into force at the beginning of November this year.

World.title: Value of Fiscalised Receipts Up By 17% in Croatia in August
World.content:
September the 4th, 2026 – The value of fiscalised receipts and invoices was up by 17% in August across Croatia. This was specifically in the provision of accommodation and food prep.

Poslovni reports that in addition to the aforementioned, 274.6 million invoices were issued in total last month, which is 8.9 million or 3.3 percent more than a year earlier. The value of fiscalised invoices rose strongly in August, while the growth in their number was considerably more moderate. Across all activities covered by the fiscalisation system, the value of issued invoices reached 6.56 billion euros, which is 17 percent or 955.3 million euros more than in the same month last year, according to data from the Tax Administration.

At the same time, 274.6 million invoices were issued last month, 8.9 million or 3.3 percent more than a year earlier. The data thus show that the average value of invoices grew noticeably faster than their number. The largest share of turnover relates to wholesale and retail trade and the repair of motor vehicles and motorcycles. In that activity, 169.9 million invoices were fiscalised, 2.6 percent or 4.25 million more than last year, while their value increased by 7.8 percent, or 258.1 million euros, to 3.56 billion euros.

In hospitality and tourism, i.e. the activity of providing accommodation and the preparation and serving of food, the number of fiscalised invoices rose by six percent to 65.7 million euros. Their value at the same time increased by 10.3 percent or 164.5 million euros, reaching 1.8 billion euros. The data refer to the period from the 1st to the 31st of August 2026 and cover all activities included in the Tax Administration’s fiscalisation system.

World.title: Dog Pennu finds a home after 1,497 days in Tartu shelter
World.content:
This spring, the dog Pennu, who had lived for more than four years at the Tartu shelter for homeless animals, found his real home.

"Just like with people, some simply don't get lucky in life — the right one just doesn't come," shelter director Annika Mölder said, explaining why Pennu spent so many years waiting for a home.

In the end, he was taken home by shelter volunteer Elisabeth Kaldvee. Kaldvee has been a volunteer at the shelter for seven years, but with Pennu it was not love at first sight at all. At first, her heart was won by the dog boy living next to Pennu.

"Pennu kept jumping like a bat onto the fence and waited for scratches under the arm. Then I just tossed treats to him, but didn't pay much attention. He wasn't my main dog to work with. I went walking with him for the first time about three years ago," Kaldvee recalled.

Dog arrived after bite incident

Pennu arrived at the shelter from a home where he had bitten another dog and a child. "Right now it seems impossible," said Mölder. "The situation was probably such that the child was with the dog, and the dogs got into a conflict with each other, and maybe the child ended up in between. The owner then decided that he did not want to keep such an aggressive dog — too big a responsibility, which is also true."

Kaldvee recalled that when Pennu arrived at the shelter, it was clear that not much work had been done with him, because he had no habit of walking on a leash, he didn't know tricks, and contact with people was minimal. He was also very reactive toward other dogs. "A lot of work and training has been done."

Kaldvee has loved dogs her whole life. As a child, she constantly asked her parents to get her a dog, but it never happened. Now she sees that her parents acted correctly, because at that time it wasn't the right moment and she didn't know enough about dogs.

Volunteer becomes owner

"But the interest has always been there. A classmate invited me to the shelter when I was 18. We went together. For her it was the last time, I kept going. Especially when you choose one dog there to focus on, it's a bit like cheating, because you start feeling like you have your own dog," Kaldvee smiled.

Becoming attached to an animal waiting for a home at the shelter can also bring great heartbreak.

"I always like to say that my first heartbreak was at the shelter, when the first dog I seriously fell in love with was adopted. His name is Bruno. I mourned him for three months and took a break from the shelter. It's a bittersweet moment, because you're happy, but on the other hand he was a dog I invested so much in. It's hard to accept that he's no longer at the shelter," Kaldvee admitted.

Years of attachment grow

Why no one wanted Pennu, Kaldvee has thought about for years. At one point she even began to hope a little that no one would take Pennu, so she could adopt him herself at the right moment.

"He is such a cool‑natured dog. He is super friendly," the owner praised. "He is the first shelter dog I have seriously trained. It was a bit sad to think that all the work I had done would go to waste and I'd have to start from scratch with another dog. And also, when you work with a dog for three years straight, you grow together. He became my dog some time ago already. The shelter workers had long been asking when I would take Pennu home."

Pennu has accepted his new home very well.

Kaldvee encourages others to adopt older dogs too, because then you don't have to worry about puppy‑like mischief. "Once they get used to the home environment, they practically sleep the whole day."

World.title: Gallery: The youth film 'Morten' premiered at Kosmos cinema
World.content:
On Friday evening, director Ivan Pavljutškov's feature‑length directorial debut "Morten" premiered at Kosmos cinema in Tallinn. The film is based on Estonian writer Reeli Reinaus' award‑winning youth novel "Morten, Emilie ja kadunud maailmad" (Morten, Emilie and the Lost Worlds).

The film's main character, Morten, cannot find his place in the school environment — exclusion and pressure from classmates make him increasingly and painfully question where he belongs and who he really is. When two girls appear in Morten's life — Miia, who is involved in street art, and the mysterious bog girl Emilie — he finds himself between two worlds and painful choices.

The title role is played by Tõru Kannimäe. Other roles are performed by Helena Maria Reisner and Emili Rohumaa, Külli Teetamm, Andres Mähar, Priit Loog and others.

The screenwriter of "Morten" is Reeli Reinaus and the director is Ivan Pavljutškov. The film's cinematographer is Ants Tammik, composer Titas Petrikis, sound designer Jonas Jocys, editor Ričardas Matačius, production designer Ketlin Kasar, costume designer Neoon Must and makeup artist Kelli Neitsov.

The film was produced by Kopli Kinokompanii together with Lithuanian co‑producer Fralita Films. The producer is Anneli Ahven, and the co‑producer is Zivile Gallego.

World.title: Ninth Station Narva festival underway in Narva
World.content:
The annual music and city festival Station Narva began in Narva on Friday, bringing well‑known performers from Estonia and abroad to the border city for a weekend of concerts and events.

The heart of the Station Narva festival, held for the ninth year, is again the Narva Castle. The festival's main stage is located in the castle's Northern Courtyard. In total, more than 20 artists will perform before the audience over two days.

Activity in the castle until at least midnight, after‑parties at the Ro‑Ro club until morning. So in fact, it would be possible to come from any corner of Estonia for at least one concert.

"I probably cannot leave unmentioned that tonight here at the Narva Museum, around midnight, the evening will be closed by the trip‑hop legend Tricky. In addition, this year's phenomenal Estonian success band SADU, and it is definitely worth lending an ear to our young modern electronic music producers Luurel Varas and Boipepperoni, who are perhaps publicly, perhaps secretly the authors of half of Estonia's Spotify Top 10 hits," said the festival's program curator Ingrid Kohtla.

"After midnight, at the Ro‑Ro club, you can see probably the coolest new‑generation Estonian punk band Skoone and also a new alternative music figure, Säde Semper," Kohtla added.

This year's festival will also feature Propeller, Tõnu Naissoo, Havryl Sydoryk, Mariin K., Malla, GusGus, Alika, Eik, Mihkel Kuusk, Planeet and others.

The festival runs until Sunday, 6 September.

World.title: Mart Võrklaev: How Estonia's public finances reached their current state
World.content:
It is extremely cynical to hear concern about budget balance from those who themselves have been the architects of irresponsible decisions, writes Mart Võrklaev in response to Jüri Ratas' commentary "Growth bought with state debt will clip future prosperity."

Jüri Ratas writes in his opinion piece "Growth bought with state debt will clip future prosperity" that Estonia needs an honest and responsible long-term view. I agree with him one hundred percent; indeed, it is time to stop telling embellished stories and look at the real situation. But to restore an honest view, we must recall how Estonia's public finances reached their current state and who is actually responsible for it.

When Jüri Ratas writes about "empty promises" in improving the budget, it is, to put it mildly, ironic. It is worth recalling what kind of legacy his government left to Kaja Kallas when handing over the leadership of the state.

The then state budget strategy contained nearly one billion euros' worth of unfunded cut promises. This was not a "long-term view," but inaction, in which it was hoped that the next government would patch up these omissions and holes. The current accusations about "empty promises" are therefore a reflection of his own actions — or more precisely, inaction.

Under Ratas' leadership, reserves were spent in good times

If we look at the deficit and surplus chart, we clearly see that the credibility of public finances did not disappear overnight. Taavi Rõivas handed over the baton in 2016 with a sound budget. From there on, during Jüri Ratas' first government and then the EKRE, Isamaa and Center Party coalition, a financial feast began, where spending was done as if there were no tomorrow. Instead of building reserves in good times, fixed costs were inflated and a systemic deficit was created.

In 2020, the EKRE–Isamaa–Center government under Jüri Ratas made a massive 5.4‑percent deficit, and Estonia's debt burden doubled in a single year. This is the "legacy" that later governments under Kaja Kallas and Kristen Michal have had to patch with difficult decisions. We have been pushed into a situation where, in addition to dealing with various crises, we have had to simultaneously reduce the budget deficit that previous governments so recklessly expanded.

This has had a direct impact on the economy as well. If the state had retained larger reserves from earlier years, we would not have had to cope in recent years simultaneously with unexpected crises, rapidly rising defense spending, and patching earlier budget holes.

This would have meant a smaller need for savings and tax changes and left more breathing room for the economy. In other words, Estonia's economic growth could have been higher in difficult times if we had not had to fix mistakes made in the past on top of new crises.

Ratas criticizes debt but is silent about what has been the main source of budget pressure in recent years. That is security. In 2022, when Estonia's security situation changed due to Russia's full‑scale aggression, raising defense spending immediately from two percent to three percent of GDP was unavoidable.

"In addition to dealing with various crises, we have had to simultaneously reduce the budget deficit that previous governments so recklessly expanded."

Comparing 2022 and 2026, we have raised defense spending from 700 million euros to more than 2.2 billion euros. This is an investment in our independence, not a convenience choice. If we still had the reserves that were spent during Ratas' governments, we would have significantly more "gunpowder" to respond to crises.

Crocodile tears vs. real actions

It is extremely cynical to hear concern about budget balance from those who themselves have been the architects of irresponsible decisions. We remember well how, during the 2023 budget negotiations, partners — including from Ratas' current home party Isamaa — pushed through unfunded promises, inflating public‑sector wage costs and indexing benefits without a long‑term financing plan.

Opposition criticism is also deeply contradictory, because on the one hand there is talk about reducing the state budget deficit, while on the other hand there are demands to increase benefits, expand bureaucracy, and abolish taxes. This is political populism.

Unlike the opposition's slogans, we have a plan based on real actions. Since 2023, we have made decisions amounting to more than one billion euros in savings. This consistent work has borne fruit. In 2024 and 2025, we have managed to reduce the budget deficit purposefully, by 1.1 and 2 percent of GDP respectively.

This trend would have continued if there had not been an urgent need to raise defense spending even more sharply to more than five percent of GDP starting in early 2026. As a result, the budget deficit also increased to more than four percent of GDP.

Going forward, we have a clear plan to continue fixing the state budget while keeping defense spending at least at five percent of GDP. The budget position must be improved by 0.5 percent of GDP per year until the state's debt burden stabilizes at 30 percent of GDP. We will do this through consistent savings in state expenditures and more efficient operations. This is certainly not an easy task, but from the perspective of responsible public finances, it is essential and realistic.

Sound finances are a guarantee of security for a small state; we must have "gunpowder" to respond in difficult times. This requires building reserves in good times. It was precisely under Jüri Ratas' leadership that these reserves were spent, bringing us a larger budget deficit, a more difficult situation in responding to crises, weaker economic resilience, and also a higher debt burden and interest costs for the future. If Jüri Ratas truly wants an honest long-term view, then that view should begin with his own mirror, not only with the podium.

World.title: Photos: Pärnu continues flood recovery as crews pump out water
World.content:
In the city of Pärnu, work continued on Saturday to eliminate the consequences of the flooding that hit the city on Friday, with the most critical situation in the beach district and the Rääma neighborhood.

According to the Pärnu city government, rescue work continues and Rescue Board teams are continuing to pump water from flooded areas into the Pärnu River.

"By morning, the water level across the entire Rääma area has dropped by about 25 centimeters. As a number, it may seem like a small change, but it has a significant impact on the residents of the area: hundreds of households where water was still inside the house last night have by morning been freed from the water trap, and residents can begin assessing the first damages," the city government wrote on social media.

At the same time, it was emphasized that the danger has not yet fully passed.

Major operations continue in several areas

Rescue Board said on Saturday that major operations in Pärnu are taking place in the Rääma oja area, around Sinioja in Paikuse, and on Pärnu maantee in the town of Sindi. Preparations are underway for pumping in the Tammiste residential district.

According to the agency's forecast, pumping operations will continue for at least another 24 hours, until Sunday under current conditions.

In Pärnu, additional teams from across Estonia are assisting local professional and volunteer rescue crews. Extra pumping resources have arrived from Elva, Iisaku, Tallinn, Muuga, Rakvere and Valga. The technical rescue unit of the Rescue Association has also been involved.

According to the head of Pärnu's crisis committee, rescuers have arrived from Tallinn, Rapla, Valga and Paide, Tõstamaa and Haapsalu.

"There has not been a rescue operation of this scale in Pärnu for a long time, and I want to personally thank every man and woman. In the morning, the brigades will rotate, but this does not mean the work will stop — far from it. Work continues so that all our people are freed from the water trap," said crisis committee head Sander Kilk.

Some streets are still closed

Due to water pumping, Õuna, Männi, Raba and Rääma tänav were closed before noon, and bus traffic in the area was rerouted.

The city government asks drivers to be especially attentive and follow safety rules.

The city government also calls on people to follow the Rescue Board's instructions, according to which electricity must be switched off immediately if water enters a building, flooded substations and electrical devices and cables must be avoided, and items that may be damaged or cause water contamination (chemicals, fuel) must be lifted off the ground.

Pärnu was hit on Friday morning by intense rainfall, which overloaded the sewer system and therefore flooded the city's streets and roads, and water also entered buildings. The amount of precipitation exceeded 100 mm, in places surpassing 120 mm.

World.title: Police to keep assisting fallen seniors outside working hours
World.content:
The Ministry of the Interior has changed its initial decision , under which police officers would no longer have to go help elderly people who have fallen at home, leaving this to ambulance crews and social workers, and has now announced that it will temporarily continue providing this assistance outside working hours.

The Ministry of the Interior's decision to stop providing this service came as a surprise to local governments and the Ministry of Social Affairs.

Starting 1 September, elderly people who have fallen at home must be helped by ambulance crews and social workers from local governments. Both the Ministry of Social Affairs and local governments say they are unable to fulfill the obligation set by the Ministry of the Interior.

Tuuli Räim. Source: Ministry of Interior

Excessive workload and lack of resources are among the reasons why such a decision was made, said Tuuli Räim, deputy secretary general of the Ministry of the Interior.

"Police resources are limited. If the police deal with responding to calls for social assistance, it may happen that somewhere else, where they definitely need to be, it becomes harder for them to reach. There are two issues. One is the competence to assess a person's health condition. The other is that we do not consider it appropriate that an armed police patrol is by default the first responding resource. That is why we have made these decisions," the deputy secretary general said.

Räim emphasized that a solution must be found to the problem. She added that since this concerns the social field, the primary responsibility lies with the Ministry of Social Affairs and the Ministry of Regional Affairs in cooperation with the Association of Cities and Municipalities. The Ministry of the Interior sees itself rather as a partner, Räim noted.

Veikko Luhalaid Autor/allikas: Raul Mee

The fact remains, however, that local governments are not yet able to take on the entire workload. According to Veikko Luhalaid, head of the Association of Estonian Cities and Municipalities, concerns include the protection of personal and health data, the inability to keep social workers on call around the clock in all municipalities, and their lack of authority to break open a home's door.

The role of local governments would primarily be to prevent falls. The analysis showed that nearly 40 percent of falls were repeat cases — meaning police had gone several times to the same home to help the same person up.

The Ministry of the Interior is now offering temporary relief: "During working hours — Monday to Friday from nine to five — assistance is organized by the local government. Outside working hours, national emergency resources will continue responding for now, whether ambulance, police or rescue services," Räim said.

World.title: Presidential office director laid off 13 staff over two years
World.content:
Office of the President Director Krista Zibo has laid off 13 staff members over the past two years, with two protocol advisers departing this Friday — barely a month before the new president takes office. Zibo herself recently secured a permanent contract.

Nearly two years ago, at President Alar Karis' proposal, Krista Zibo — formerly with the Government Office — became director of the Office of the President.

"Her previous professional path has given her balance and strong experience in leading different teams, as well as a clear understanding of topics important to Estonia, which I saw confirmed when we worked together at the National Audit Office," Karis said at the time.

Two employees — advisers in the office's protocol field, Pille Heinsoo and Sigrid Herodes — had their last working day this Friday. This is only about a month before the new president, Ülle Madise, takes office.

Layoffs justified by a structural change

"A structural change was what they told us," Herodes said sadly, adding that she herself would also like to know what the exact reason for the layoff is. She said that tasks were redistributed in the office, meaning the work done by Herodes and Heinsoo will not remain undone.

Herodes noted that it remained unclear to her what will happen to her position. "In my opinion, it is disappearing now," she said. When asked whether 13 layoffs in two years is a lot, Herodes answered yes.

Zibo said in an emailed comment that the office is changing its work organization according to the president's needs.

"In recent years, changes have been made both in support functions and in the circle of advisers to the head of state — tasks have been redistributed, work roles changed and responsibilities consolidated," Zibo noted. She added that the personnel changes made are part of this process and stem from changes in work tasks and the need to use the office's limited resources more efficiently.

Office building of the President of Estonia. Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

Layoff patterns also exist from earlier

One of the best‑known people Zibo had laid off from the presidential office was then‑presidential adviser Toomas Sildam. This happened in February 2025, only about five months after Zibo became director. "The domestic policy adviser's duties will be taken over by the domestic policy department," the office announced at the time.

Layoff issues also followed Zibo at the Government Office, where she worked before becoming director of the Presidential Office. In 2019, ERR wrote that the Government Office laid off protocol chief Ülle‑Marika Põldma, who had worked in that position for more than ten years. At the time, Zibo, who worked as head of support services at the Government Office, also commented that Põldma was laid off due to work reorganization.

Allegedly, the reason for the layoff was poor cooperation, but the Government Office did not officially confirm this. Similar to the current situation in the Office of the President, the Government Office did not hire a new person as protocol chief at that time.

Krista Zibo. Source: Government Office

The director received a €10,500 bonus

The staff is not the only thing changing in the office before the new president's term begins. For nearly two years, Zibo held the director's position under a fixed‑term contract (a fixed‑term transfer from the Government Office). As of 1 July this year, Zibo is permanently on staff.

In a letter forwarded by presidential office's spokesperson, it was explained that the task of the office director is to ensure the continuity of the institution's work, including during a presidential transition. If the new president wishes to see someone else as director of the office, a new person can be hired in place of Zibo.

When asked why the contract was changed only now — a few months before Karis's term ends — the office replied that Zibo must ensure stable leadership and daily work of the office until the end of Karis's term and during the presidential transition. Whether this could not have been done with a fixed‑term transfer contract was not clarified in the response.

"President Alar Karis and his team will carry out their duties fully until the end of the term," the letter stated. It added that the incoming president will in turn have the opportunity to shape their team of advisers.

President Karis appears clearly satisfied with the director's work. On 29 January this year, Alar Karis issued an order setting Krista Zibo's new base salary at €6,010 per month starting 1 January 2026. Previously her salary was €5,500. When she took office on 2 September 2024, it was €5,000.

On 24 November 2025, Alar Karis decided to pay Zibo a €10,500 bonus for good service‑related achievements.

World.title: Video: Emergency situation declared in Pärnu after heavy rain floods streets
World.content:
A crisis situation was declared Friday in Pärnu after record rainfall — described as the rain of the century — caused widespread flooding, overwhelmed sewers and forced school closures.

The Pärnu city government wrote around 8:30 a.m. Friday that the very large amount of rain that has fallen in the last few hours has placed a heavy burden on the sewage system and that the system is operating at full capacity.

"Unfortunately, both stormwater drainage and sewerage services have been disrupted, and in many places roads are difficult to pass due to water accumulation," the city noted.

The city government asked motorists to be careful and avoid flooded roads. The city and service providers worked to resolve the situation. "The situation is really difficult," the city's post read.

Water in the yard of a private residence in Rääma on Saturday. Source: Kristi Raidla / ERR

Water pumping continued Saturday in Pärnu

On Friday evening and on Saturday, rescue work and pumping out rainwater continued in Pärnu.

In the evening, the city of Pärnu announced on social media that the most critical situation is in the areas of Rääma, Ehitajate tee, Savi tänav and Raba tänav, and that the work of the pumps will certainly create noise.

"A huge, huge thank‑you to all the rescuers! Additional help has arrived in Pärnu from all over Estonia," the city said.

Amount of rain was exceptional

Meteorologist Kairo Kiitsak reported that as of 9:20 a.m. Friday, an exceptionally large amount of rain had fallen in Pärnu and its surrounding areas. Rainfall totals exceeded 100 mm, and in some places passed the 120 mm mark.

Heavy rainfall will continue during the day, especially in southwestern, central and eastern Estonia.

Rääma school sent the children home

Pärnu Rääma School announced on Friday morning that there will be no classes at the school due to heavy rain.

"The sewage system and toilets are not working and the lowest floor is covered in water," said Elmo Joa, principal of the Rääma school, adding that the children are being sent home.

Joa told ERR that they are currently waiting for a pump to remove the water from the basement floor.

"We're all doing well now. The children were coming to school. A lot of the younger ones who came with their parents were able to go back at the door because rubber boots would be suitable as a change of shoes. So they went back home nicely. They were very sad because it was raining outside and it wasn't raining inside. It was exciting here," said Joa.

Deputy mayor: We are declaring an emergency

Pärnu Deputy Mayor Sander Kilk said in a comment to ERR that after the crisis committee met, the city decided to declare a state of emergency.

"Since this water probably won't go away for several hours, there could be damage to property. Another thing we have a problem with are the sewer hatches that have come loose. The sewers can't handle this water, so they are dangerous if people drive cars, bicycles, or walk there," said Kilk.

According to Kilk, this is the first time that such a large flood caused by rainwater has occurred in Pärnu. It also became clear that the city was not prepared for such a crisis situation.

"Right now, the first goal is to resolve today's situation calmly and then we'll look ahead. It turned out that no previous city government has compiled a crisis manual, so to speak. We will definitely do that, and not just in the event of a small crisis, but also in all other possible cases. However, a staff has been put together, including department heads who are currently dealing with it, and we ourselves," said Kilk.

According to the deputy mayor, we currently have to wait for the rainfall to decrease or stop. Then we can start pumping water out of people's basements. In addition, the Pärnu Rescue Association is helping.

The Rescue Board has activated the regional headquarters and is implementing the flood emergency plan activities, supporting the local government. To the Board's knowledge, no lives are in danger.

Water entered the barrier at Pärnu Hospital

Tõnno Sikk, field manager of the Western Rescue Center, said on Vikerraadio's "Uudis+" program that it has been a very busy time for rescue resources.

"We have visited various sites, and there have been reports from private individuals where water has penetrated the basement. We have had to prioritize the events and have provided assistance to both Pärnu Hospital and some elementary schools. We are currently mapping the situation to identify the sites that need our help most urgently," said Sikk.

Water entered one of the locks at Pärnu Hospital, but the situation was brought under control in cooperation with the hospital.

"We also visited Rääma Primary School, where water threatened to flood the server room. We installed barriers there, and volunteer resources also helped ensure that the school did not have to close its doors for an extended period of time," said Sikk.

Pumping water out of Rääma school. Source: Kristi Raidla / ERR

Professor: This could be called the rain of the century

According to Ottar Tamm, a junior professor at the Estonian University of Life Sciences, measurements have shown that intense rainfall is occurring more and more frequently and there is no reason to believe that this will be different in the future.

"In one hour, 33 millimeters of rain fell in Pärnu, which statistically occurs about once every seven years. In two hours, a total of 56 millimeters fell, which happens once every 22 years, and in six hours, once every 77 years. These are absolute values, but there is a lot of margin, so it can be completely freely called the rain of the century," said Tamm.

While citizens often demand that after every major flood, the municipality should build thicker sewer pipes and dig wider drainage ditches, hydrological scientists do not consider this a good solution.

"We need to do something on the ground to retain this rainwater. This involves nature-based rainwater solutions, where we delay the water. In the case of Pärnu, we are primarily talking about delay, not impregnation - we consciously keep the water in the places where we want it. If we don't keep it there, the water chooses its own flow path and inevitably the lowest place is often the basement," explained Tamm.

According to the researcher, Tallinn has worked hard and addressed the problem, compiling stormwater models and assessing where water collects and where problems arise. Tartu and elsewhere in Estonia have not seen any progress on Tamm.

"Today is a very good example of how we will not get anywhere by continuing as we have been, because there will be more and more such situations in the future. We must be prepared for this, or else society will have to accept that we will start to drown more - this is also actually a solution, but it just needs to be acknowledged," said Tamm.

Several tunnels closed in the Pärnu region

Due to heavy rainfall, the section of Audru Road under the Audru viaduct at km 0.5 is currently closed in Pärnu, as are the pedestrian tunnels under Ehitajate Road in the city of Pärnu, which have remained underwater.

The road maintenance officer and the pump station maintenance officer are inspecting the condition of the tunnels. The necessary traffic signs have been placed on site and the pump station technician is checking the condition of the pumps.

All the tunnel pumps have been operating at full capacity since early Friday morning, but the amount of rainwater has been exceptionally high, and therefore it will take time to pump out the water from the tunnels and dry them.

The rain has started to subside and the situation is expected to return to normal by the evening. The tunnels will remain closed until it is safe to use them again.

In addition to Pärnu, flooding may also occur in other regions. According to the Environment Agency, rainfall will continue in Pärnu County and move across to Virumaa in Järva County.

Editor's note: This piece was updated to include the declaration of an emergency situation in Pärnu, activation of the Rescue Board's regional headquarters, water entering Pärnu Hospital, the "rain of the century" assessment, and the closure of tunnels due to flooding.

World.title: Integrity probes liquidity drain and 1B+ dinar loans at Rafidain and Rasheed
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Federal Commission of Integrity and specialized judicial oversight bodies have launched a comprehensive financial audit and investigative probe into liquidity depletion, high-value commercial loans, and discretionary financing waivers across Iraq’s state-owned banking sector on Saturday, September 5, 2026.

The investigation centers on operational practices at Rafidain Bank and Rasheed Bank—the country’s two dominant state lenders—examining major credit facilities exceeding 1 billion IQD (approximately $763,000) granted through non-standard channels or exceptional exemptions.

According to sources close to the regulatory authorities, forensic teams are cross-referencing credit files against statutory central bank lending guidelines to determine civil and administrative culpability:

High-Value Credit Facilities:Scrutinizing loans and investment financing packages valued from 1 billion IQD upward, assessing whether underwriting criteria and collateral coverage adhered to regulatory standards.

Beneficiary Audits:Examining corporate structures, political affiliations, and corporate vehicles granted special exemptions, verifying whether funds were directed toward actual commercial assets or converted into speculative cash holdings.

Historical Policy Tracing: Multiple files under scrutiny date back to policies and executive administrative approvals issued under the previous cabinet and Ministry of Finance administration.

Misleading Administrative Disclosures: Following up on reports from late August indicating that some bank boards submitted inaccurate or misleading liquidity statements to senior government leadership amid delays in civil service payroll allocations.

Core Areas of the Banking Investigation

Audit Focus Investigation Target Regulatory Objective Credit Packages ≥ 1B IQD Commercial facilities, corporate overdrafts, and project finance Confirm collateral solvency and compliance with statutory lending ceilings. Special Clearances Ministerial waivers and board-level discretionary exemptions Identify irregular approvals granted outside standard central bank risk frameworks. Liquidity Outflows Depletion of cash reserves at Rafidain & Rasheed Trace capital drains that hindered timely public salary disbursements. Corporate Beneficiaries Corporate borrowers, contracting partners, and individuals Verify capital deployment in licensed projects versus capital flight or diversion.

The timing of the banking probe reflects wider liquidity strains on the Iraqi treasury, where public compensation and social welfare spending average over 7.4 trillion IQD monthly:

World.title: Iraq achieves wheat and date self-sufficiency for 2026: Agriculture Ministry
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture announced on Friday, September 4, 2026, that Iraq has achieved full self-sufficiency in its strategic wheat harvest for the third consecutive season, while also securing complete domestic self-sufficiency in date production.

Ministry Spokesperson Qusay Al-Hattab stated that targeted state interventions—combining climate-resilient crop genetics, subsidized modern sprinkler systems, and a data-backed agricultural calendar—have decoupled key food staples from volatile international import markets.

Core Pillars of Agricultural Self-Sufficiency

Three Consecutive Seasons of Wheat Sufficiency: The 2026 winter harvest solidified a three-year streak of domestic grain self-reliance, with the ministry already preparing its winter crop plan to maintain full coverage into 2027.

Climate-Adaptive Seed Cultivars: Agricultural research divisions successfully introduced proprietary wheat seed strains engineered to withstand high soil salinity, prolonged drought, and extreme climatic volatility.

Subsidized Irrigation Upgrades (Austrian Loan Facility): To combat persistent water scarcity across the Tigris and Euphrates basins, modern pivot and localized sprinkler systems are distributed under a 33% state subsidy. Pivot systems valued at 70 million IQD are provided to registered farmers for 49 million IQD, financed through a 10-year installment plan with a one-year grace period.

Date Palm Sector Expansion: Iraq’s date palm population expanded from roughly 12 million trees in 2003 to 22 million trees in 2026, driven by replanting campaigns and commercial orchard developments, with Zahdi dates comprising the largest share of national yield.

Agricultural Policy Framework: Modernization and Trade Protections

Policy Instrument Operational Detail Strategic Objective Wheat Support Program Salinity-tolerant seeds + subsidized machinery Eliminate grain import dependence for the national food basket. Austrian Irrigation Loan 33% unit subsidy (49M IQD net; 10-yr financing) Transition from flood irrigation to water-efficient pivot sprinklers. Date Palm Restoration Expansion to 22 million trees Reclaim historical export capacity and achieve domestic surplus. Permanent Import Bans 33 agricultural items permanently banned Protect local vegetable and fruit producers from dumping. World.title: Iraqi judiciary completes interrogation of 5,700 ISIS suspects
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Supreme Judicial Council of Iraq has officially concluded the interrogation process for 5,704 ISIS detainees who were moved from northeastern Syria earlier this year, preparing them for trial.

The First Karkh Investigation Court said in a statement on Tuesday that it concluded the investigation phase of one of Iraq’s largest terrorism-related cases in history.

The verified detainees originate from 67 different nationalities, including 3,497 Syrians and 474 Iraqis.

The courts identified very dangerous agents in key leadership, military, financial, media, and security roles inside ISIS.

Six offenders were actively linked to the captivity, detention, transfer, sale, and exploitation of Yazidi women, exposing serious international crimes.

Several suspects have previously been cleared and released due to insufficient evidence linking them to terrorism crimes.

In 2014, the terrorist group ISIS took control of large areas in Iraq and Syria before being defeated in 2017.

Over five million Iraqis had to flee the governorates of Nineveh, Salah al-Din, parts of Kirkuk, Diyala, and Anbar because of ISIS control over these areas in 2014.

Although Iraq declared in late 2017 that all of its regions were free of ISIS, the government continues to conduct security operations to hunt out any remaining members of the terrorist group.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate rises in Baghdad, remain stable in Erbil
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar rose on Thursday in Baghdad, the Iraqi capital, and remained stable in Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,547.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,546.5 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad rose, ranging between 1,552.5 Iraqi dinars and 1,542.5 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate remained stable, fluctuating between 1,546 and 1,545.5 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation represented more than a 10 percent difference in exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq exports fuel oil through Jordan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told Attaqa News that Iraq began exporting fuel oil shipments via Jordan for the first time last month.

Al-Rikabi explained that Iraq is exporting fuel oil through the neighboring country, not to Jordan.

The Iraqi official did not disclose the details of the agreement, its duration, or when it came into effect.

Iraqi oil shipments started flowing to Jordan in early August through the Trebil border crossing, the only land border crossing between the two countries, at a rate of 10,000 barrels per day, which were stored in the facilities of the Jordan Oil Terminals Company (JOTC), Jordan’s state-owned petroleum logistics and independent storage provider.

Through Jordan, a shipment totaling 307,000 barrels was exported to Greece.

Following the Strait of Hormuz crisis, which began with the United States’ war against Iran on February 28, Iraqi fuel oil shipments began transiting through Syria via tanker trucks, with storage at the Baniyas refinery before shipping to worldwide markets.

Between March and the end of August, Iraq exported 21.4 million barrels of fuel oil through Syria and only 307,000 barrels through Jordan.

Iraqi fuel oil exports started to increase following the Middle East conflict until the end of August in an attempt to compensate for the declining supplies via the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: 38 officers, 3,000 personnel dismissed over corruption in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Interior announced on Thursday that it permanently dismissed 38 officers and 180 personnel over administrative and financial corruption, with another 3,245 personnel discharged for desertion.

The purge represents a significant internal effort as part of the ongoing “Operation Dawn,” a nationwide anti-corruption campaign spearheaded by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s government. The campaign has targeted numerous public officials and high-profile individuals.

According to an official statement from Miqdad Miri, the spokesperson for the Interior Ministry, the total number of individuals affected encompasses various categories of misconduct.

After receiving clear evidence of their direct involvement in bribery and financial misconduct, 38 officers were permanently removed from service.

Finalized judicial verdicts convicting 180 enlisted personnel of corruption accusations resulted in their official removal from service.

As part of larger ministry attempts to reestablish strong institutional discipline, 3,245 service personnel were discharged only for abandoning their duties.

These dismissals took place within the first 100 days of the current government’s tenure.

This security-sector cleanup is part of the larger nationwide drive “Operation Dawn.” Between late June and August, security operations resulted in the arrest of at least 210 lawmakers, public servants, and business executives.

World.title: CIL offers extra fuel, 57 plants now report critically low stock
World.content:
NEW DELHI: State-run Coal India Limited (CIL) has offered power plants having fuel supply agreements with it and its subsidiaries to lift additional quantities of coal, over and above the quantities stipulated in their annual contracts, as stocks available at thermal power plants fell further.

Central Electricity Authority (CEA) data showed that on Sept 4, the number of plants with critically low coal stocks had increased to 57. The total stock availability was estimated at 27.1 MT, or 47% of the recommended requirement of 57.7 MT. TOI Saturday reported that 50 of 190 coal-fired power plants had less than 25% of the recommended coal requirement.

Coal ministry said the situation was likely to improve now as intense rains over coal command regions showed clear signs of easing, while production and supplies of the fuel at CIL's mines were gathering pace.

"Despite prolonged spells of rain through July and Aug, particularly across the East-Central parts, CIL maintained a steady supply run. During April-Aug of the current fiscal, CIL supplied 322.9 MT of coal, 6.7% higher than the 302.6 MT supplied during the corresponding period last year."

World.title: Panun Kashmir stages hunger strike, demands genocide law
World.content:
JAMMU: A displaced Kashmiri Pandit organisation Saturday observed a day-long hunger strike demanding the creation of a separate homeland in the valley for their rehabilitation and enactment of a genocide law.

Panun Kashmir chairperson Tito Ganju said India, as a signatory to the UN Genocide Convention, was obligated to enact a dedicated law dealing with genocide.

The organisationâs demands included official recognition of the genocide of Kashmiri Pandits, passage of a Genocide Bill, creating a separate Union Territory as a secure homeland in the valley, creation of 15,000 jobs in central govt departments for unemployed and over-aged youth, and enhancement of ex gratia assistance and monthly relief.

World.title: NTPC, Talcher Fertilisers apply under Rs 37,500cr coal gasification scheme
World.content:
NEW DELHI: At least two companies - state-run NTPC and public sector JV Talcher Fertilisers - have submitted applications under the Rs 37,500-crore surface coal and lignite gasification projects scheme, govt said on Saturday.

It added that the coal ministry is also in touch with more prospective applicants who are at various stages of project preparation and finalising their applications.

The ministry also dismissed reports suggesting that the scheme had failed to attract potential investors. âGiven the significant scale and complexity of the projects envisaged under the scheme, prospective applicants are required to undertake substantial preparatory work, including preparation of pre-feasibility reports, assessment of technology options, identification of coal/lignite and other feedstock arrangements, evaluation of project economics and preparation of detailed project proposals.

It is therefore expected that additional applicants may finalise and submit their proposals as the deadline approaches,â the ministry said in a statement.

Aimed at promoting the conversion of domestic coal and lignite into higher-value products such as syngas, methanol, ammonia and urea, the scheme was approved by the Cabinet in May this year, while the coal ministry floated the request for proposal in July. The last date for submitting applications in the first round is Sept 7.





The initiative is expected to catalyse investments of Rs 2.5-3 lakh crore across nearly 25 projects and generate around 50,000 direct and indirect employment opportunities.

India is aiming to gasify 100 million tonnes of coal by 2030.

Under the Rs 8,500-crore coal gasification scheme launched in 2024, eight projects with a combined capacity of nearly 22.6 million tonnes per annum have been approved. One project, being executed by Jindal Steel Limited, is under construction, while another, awarded to Talcher Fertilisers, is in the initial stages.

World.title: Punjab combines drug enforcement with addiction treatment in anti-narcotics drive
World.content:
File photo: Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann

Arrests and drug seizures

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Police intervention in addiction treatment

Information received through Punjabâs Safe Punjab Helpline has contributed to 25,339 arrests in drug-related cases since the state launched its âYudh Nashean Virudhâ campaign in March 2025, according to data released by the Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF).Between March 1, 2025, and September 3, 2026, the helpline received 51,979 tip-offs from citizens about suspected drug peddling and other drug-related activities.The data showed that 59,293 FIRs had been registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act in Punjab during the period.Authorities said more than 25,000 arrests resulted from information received through the helpline.The enforcement drive also resulted in the arrest of 696 people who were found with more than 2 kg of heroin each, according to the data.Authorities reported recovering 3,757 kg of heroin, 964 kg of opium, 45 tonnes of poppy husk, 1,288 kg of ganja and 71 kg of methamphetamine, commonly known as ICE.They also recovered 62 lakh tablets and capsules in cases registered under the NDPS Act.The operation resulted in the seizure of Rs 22 crore in suspected drug-related money. A total of 2,675 cases involving commercial quantities of drugs were also registered.Punjab DGP Gaurav Yadav said citizen tip-offs had assisted the ANTF and expected further participation.âTip-offs have provided extra teeth to the Anti-Narcotics Task Force and we firmly believe that in the days to come, there will be more citizen participation in giving tip-offs and subsequent arrests as a result of it,â Yadav said.ADGP ANTF Punjab Nilabh Kishore said the figures showed that information from citizens was being used alongside enforcement action.âThe figures suggest that the anti-drug campaign is increasingly combining enforcement action with citizen-generated intelligence. The over 51,979 tip-offs received through the helpline indicate that members of the public are actively feeding information into the enforcement mechanism,â Kishore said.The data also covers police efforts to connect people struggling with addiction to treatment services.According to the figures, police took 42,498 people to de-addiction centres, while another 1,55,970 people were taken to Outpatient Opioid Assisted Treatment (OOAT) clinics.Separately, 11,239 individuals were granted immunity under Section 64A of the NDPS Act. The provision provides protection in specified circumstances to drug-dependent people who voluntarily undergo treatment.The figures released by the state therefore cover both enforcement against drug-related activities and police-assisted access to treatment for people struggling with addiction.
