The complainant alleged that posts from the minorâs X account contained derogatory references to Bhagwan Shiv, Bhagwan Shri Krishna, Maa Saraswati and Maa Durga.âI am a practising Hindu. I viewed the posts listed below on X (formerly Twitter) while at the Supreme Court of India, New Delhi. The posts remain publicly available and have outraged my religious feelings and those of other Hindus,â news agency ANI reported Sachdeva saying.Sachdeva has sought registration of an FIR under Sections 299 and 196 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), besides applicable provisions of the Information Technology Act, 2000.According to the complaint, four posts uploaded between September 2023 and August 2026 allegedly insulted Hindu deities and religious beliefs. Sachdeva alleged the posts were published with deliberate and malicious intent to âoutrage the religious feelingsâ of Hindus.She said she had earlier sought their removal but they remained online.The lawyer has sought preservation of the posts, associated media and platform records, including IP logs, device details and other electronic evidence. She has also sought steps to prevent further circulation of the alleged content.The complaint is separate from an alleged assault case involving the minorâs father during a CJP protest at Jantar Mantar in July. CJP has accused self-styled influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj of assaulting him, while Bhardwaj has claimed the incident was an act of self-defence.Bhardwaj was detained by Delhi Police on Friday from Bulandshahr and was remanded to one day of police custody after being produced before a court in Delhi on Saturday.

World.title: Abhayrab vials found in Delhi flagged as substandard
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Vials labelled as Abhayrab, a rabies vaccine, found at an unlicensed residential premises in Mukherjee Nagar have been declared âNot of Standard Qualityâ and misbranded by the Central Drugs Laboratory, Kasauli, with the manufacturer saying the tested vials were not its product.

The vials carried batch number KE25012 and were sampled by the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) during an enforcement action and sent to the laboratory for testing. The laboratory report recorded 17 differences between the tested vial and the retention samples of the same batch submitted by Human Biologicals Institute, a division of Indian Immunologicals Ltd, for batch-release testing.

The sample failed the potency requirement, though it passed sterility, moisture and identity tests.

Differences were also found in labelling, artwork, QR-code verification, cap colour, licence details and packaging text. Indian Immunologicals said the vials examined were not manufactured by Human Biologicals Institute.

The company said the genuine KE25012 batch had been tested and released by the Central Drugs Laboratory under a batch-release certificate dated November 7, 2025. The 83,370 vials released from the batch were supplied only through its authorised distribution channel, it said, adding that no market complaint had been received for the batch.





The development is significant because a spurious or substandard rabies vaccine may fail to provide the protection expected after an animal bite. Rabies is almost invariably fatal once clinical symptoms develop, making effective post-exposure vaccination critical.

The Delhi location is significant against the backdrop of a Crime Branch raid in Mukherjee Nagar earlier this year, in which 953 rabies vaccine vials were among medicines recovered in an alleged spurious-drug racket.

Four people were arrested. However, there is currently no evidence establishing that those seized vials were from batch KE25012.

The latest finding also comes less than two years after Indian Immunologicals informed the drug regulator in January 2025 about counterfeit Abhayrab doses carrying batch number KA24014. Health authorities in the US, UK and Australia subsequently issued alerts for people who may have received the vaccine in India.

Indian Immunologicals said it submitted its manufacturing, quality-control, reconciliation and distribution records to CDSCO on August 14. In its September 4 representation to the Drugs Controller General of India, it asked authorities to trace the source of the vials and act against those responsible.

The company said every Abhayrab batch is independently tested and released by the Central Drugs Laboratory before sale. Vaccines supplied through hospitals, clinics, government facilities and licensed pharmacies via its authorised distribution chain, it said, are not affected by the matter.

World.title: Centre finds no single cause for Balaghat child deaths
World.content:
The inquiry into the illness affecting tribal children in Balaghat revealed various clinical factors behind their conditions.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Centreâs investigation into the illness cluster among tribal children in Madhya Pradeshâs Balaghat has found multiple clinical causes among reported deaths, including measles, malaria, co-infection, respiratory distress, dehydration, malnutrition, anaemia and shock. Officials said the deaths cannot currently be attributed to a single pathogen.Senior officials in the Union health ministry said 431 children have so far been admitted to health facilities, with 379 discharged and 52 still under treatment and observation. More than 32,000 people have been screened, with surveillance expanded from three villages to around 50.A National Joint Outbreak Response Team (NJORT) was deployed on August 12, following a national review on August 4 of the epidemiological situation, reported mortality, measles and malaria findings, laboratory strategy and containment measures. An independent Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) team is also involved in the investigation.ICMR teams from Jabalpur and Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Medical College, Jabalpur, have been visiting affected areas. The investigation includes clinical and laboratory assessment, measles and malaria surveillance, mortality review and entomological investigations.Officials said several early deaths occurred at home or before patients reached an appropriate health facility, limiting the availability of clinical records and diagnostic specimens.A case-wise retrospective review, including verbal autopsies, is being undertaken.Meanwhile, 14,637 children aged 1-10 years have received an additional Measles-Rubella (MR) vaccine dose. More than 600 drinking-water sources have been purified and insecticide spraying completed in 4,338 households.Six Mobile Medical Units have been deployed in Birsa and Baihar blocks, while more than 10 doctors and 10 Community Health Officers are working in the affected areas.Screening also found 7,711 children with severe acute malnutrition, of whom 518 were admitted to Nutrition Rehabilitation Centres. Another 13,406 children with diarrhoea and 274 with severe pneumonia were identified and managed.The government said the situation is improving, with no new measles case reported in Balaghat in the past seven days. Surveillance and treatment continue, particularly in remote tribal and Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG) habitations.

World.title: 'Jhooth ki goonj': PM Modi takes swipe at Rahul, attacks 'mai-baap' culture
World.content:
'Modi stands like a rock'

PM Modi takes 'Naraz Fufa' jibe

PM recalls 2013, attacks UPA-era record

'Dimagi Naxal' remark

PM highlights handling of crises

'India is not only growing'

India's armed forces enter their territory & strike

PM praises SRCC alumni

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you agree with characterization of the Congress party outreach campaign as jhooth ki goonj? Yes, I agree No, I disagree 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday took a jibe at leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi, describing the Congress party's student outreach campaign "Chhatron Ki Goonj" as "jhooth ki goonj".'Chhatron Ki Goonj' is a student-dialogue campaign launched by the Congress to raise issues including examination paper leaks, rising education costs, irregularities in government recruitment and unemployment.Over the past three months, the campaign has been held in Kota in Rajasthan, Dehradun in Uttarakhand, Prayagraj in Uttar Pradesh and Pune in Maharashtra.Addressing the centenary celebrations of Delhi University's Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC), PM Modi said, "...Main jaanta hoon, sach ki Hunkkaar ke aage jhooth ki goonj tik nahi sakegi (I know that the echo of lies cannot stand before the roar of truth)."PM Modi said he had the courage to remind students of his 2013 speech and compare his claims with India's current position."This is Modi. He stands like a rock in front of those who favour the 'mai-baap' culture. I have the courage, which is why I am reminding you of what I said that day.I have come before you with my report card. At the same programme in 2013, when I said that we needed to work towards "Made in India," people from the ecosystem of that time simply could not understand it. They believed that Made in India was impossible during that period of despair. And those who were brought up with that mindset still make fun of Made in India today. But today you can see the brand value of Make in India,â the PM said.The Primr Minister also described those who oppose government initiatives as "Naraz Fufa", saying, "But outside this campus, you will encounter a new world. You will meet two kinds of people. One kind consists of people who positively transform the strength of society into the strength of the nation. The second kind is made up of people who become the "Naraz Fufa" whenever any work is started."Their favourite thing is to oppose everything. They have only one dialogue: What is the need for this? When we were building the world's tallest statue, the "Fufa" said, "What is the need for this?" When we started working on the high-speed train, the "Fufa" again said, What is the need for this? When we introduced UPI, these same "Fufas" asked, Why UPI? When we built the new Parliament building, they again said, "What is the need for this?" We built a memorial for our brave military heroes who dedicated their lives and made the supreme sacrifice for the country. The "Fufa" came onto the field again and asked, "What was the need for this?" But India gave an answer to all these "Fufas." No one can stop India from doing what is necessary for the country," he added.Recalling the situation in 2013, PM Modi listed what he described as the major challenges facing the country at the time."There is a gang that will take what I am saying, break it into small pieces and put it in my account. So, let me warn you in advance about this. Let me tell you what used to dominate the media during that period in 2013. For example, Indian soldiers were being killed along the LoC. The current generation may find it surprising; perhaps they may wonder, "Did this really happen?" Yes, it did. The World Bank had lowered its GDP growth forecast. The current account deficit was at an all-time high. Inflation was around 10 per cent. The industrial sector was in the grip of a slowdown. Corruption in the helicopter deal had been exposed. There were bomb blasts in Hyderabad. These were all headlines at that time. I firmly believe that our students today may not know about all these things," PM Modi said."These developments show what the condition of the country was at that time. Growth was at the bottom, while inflation was at the peak. Scams were at their height, and the corrupt were moving around fearlessly. The economy was in distress. There was discussion everywhere about policy paralysis. The world was counting India among the "Fragile Five." Terrorists were operating unchecked, and Pakistan was out of control. In other words, there was nothing but disappointment and despair. There was a time when the country was struggling on every front..." he added.PM Modi said that despite being in the opposition during his 2013 visit, he had not used the SRCC platform to attack the then government."Your seniors were sitting here in 2013, and at that time I was the Chief Minister, but I was also a member of the country's main opposition party. Perhaps people were expecting me to launch a long, strong attack on the then Central Government and level a barrage of allegations. But, even though I was in the Opposition and a critic of the government of the time, I did not use this platform for that purpose. I presented a vision. I spoke positively. Whatever I said then was my conviction. I have always lived those thoughts and dreams. I continued to follow that path, to dedicate myself wholeheartedly to the country and to have the passion to live for the nation...At that time, all of you may have been in school. But today, if you go on the internet and read the news from 2013 and around that period, you will get an idea of what the situation was like then.""My 2013 speech at SRCC had become a wave, and even today, 13-14 years later, the impact of that address remains intact," he said.PM also referred to his recent "Dimagi Naxal" remark, comparing it to a homeopathic treatment. "You may have heard my speech from Red Fort. I gave a homeopathic pill from the Red Fortâ"Dimagi Naxal". According to the principles of homeopathy, when you begin homeopathic treatment, the disease initially gets worse. That is the nature of homeopathy. Similarly, as soon as I gave the "Dimagi Naxal" homeopathic pill, all the "Dimagi Naxals" started coming out one after another. And now the public is also seeing the true colours of those who are promoting this illness," PM Modi said.The prime minister listed the challenges India had faced in recent years, including the Covid-19 pandemic, the Russia-Ukraine war and the West Asia crisis."I have told you so many things. Some people may think, "What is this? This is a country of 140 crore people. It was very easy. What new thing did Modi do?" But was it really that easy? I want to take you back to the old days once again. Remember, when you were in school, there was a disaster in Kedarnath in 2013. The entire government was shaken. They simply did not know what to do or how to respond. When the banking crisis came in 2008, the government at the time tried to hide behind the crisis for years. It did not even have the courage to tackle it," PM Modi said."The entire banking system of India was pushed to the brink of collapse. In 2008 itself, there was a horrific terror attack in Mumbai. The government of the time came under pressure from outside but did not even have the courage to teach Pakistan a lesson...Over the past six years, we have faced major crises. First came the COVID-19 pandemic, which brought the entire world to a standstill. Then the war between Russia and Ukraine broke out. After that, there was a period when trade and supply chains began to be weaponised," he added.Every time, people said, "Now India will not survive." And those who are my biggest admirers were happy, thinking, "Now Modi is trapped. Now Modi has fallen. Now they will crush him." But the blessings of the people of my country have so much strength, so much strength, that every wish of those who want India to fail is being left unfulfilled."PM Modi also highlighted India's latest economic figures, including 7.8 per cent quarterly growth, and said the country's performance showed its resilience despite global challenges."The world was calling India one of the 'Fragile Five.' Today, the world is watching India become the fastest-growing major economy. In just the past week, there have been several positive developments regarding India's economy. The 7.8 per cent quarterly growth has boosted the country's confidence. Meanwhile, a Japanese credit rating agency has upgraded India's rating. And this 7.8 per cent growth has come at a time when the war in West Asia is ongoing and there have been several trade-related challenges. Achieving such growth under these circumstances shows India's strength and potential. I know, and you also know, that those who became infamous for pushing India into the 'Fragile Five' are finding these figures difficult to digest. But all of you understand the data seriously...In other words, India is not only growing but also creating new employment opportunities. Despite this, those for whom the glass was half empty in 2013 continue to think the same way even today. For them, the glass will always be half empty. I talk about the glass; I am not talking about anything remaining empty," the PM said.PM Modi also said India's security situation had improved, citing developments in Jammu and Kashmir, the Northeast and the fight against Maoist insurgency."Today, those spreading terrorism are on the back foot. If Pakistan indulges in any misadventure, India's armed forces enter their territory and strike. Peace has increased from Jammu and Kashmir to the Northeast.""The back of Maoist terrorism and Naxalism has been broken. The world that was once concerned about India's policy paralysis is today talking about India's policy dynamism," he added.Praising SRCC and its alumni, PM Modi said the institution had produced prominent figures across fields, including economics, politics, law and the arts."The alumni of SRCC have also been very special. In your language, I would say the alumni here are the OGs. They have taken the name of SRCC across the world and made a mark for themselves in different fields. Our Arun Jaitley ji studied here. And I can say that perhaps there was hardly a meeting with him where he did not share an incident from his SRCC days. Sometimes I would get tired because he would tell me the same incident again and again. Even today, Sanjeev Sanyal, who is part of my team, is an alumnus of SRCC. We have many other colleagues who studied here as well. And it is not that SRCC has produced people only from the world of economics. From artists to politicians, lawyers and judges, people from every field have emerged from here."He also described the institution's 100-year journey as one marked by achievements and inspiration. "When a person lives for 100 years, they are considered an ocean of experience. And when an institution completes 100 years, it becomes an ocean of achievements and inspiration. In its 100-year journey, SRCC has shaped generations and connected them with a brighter future. Those who came here studied, and those who left emerged as well-shaped individuals," he added.PM Modi took a metro ride to the college and interacted with students and fellow passengers during the journey. He also released a commemorative Rs 100 coin to mark the centenary.The prime minister's visit comes amid the BJP's ongoing outreach to young voters. He had last visited SRCC in 2013, when he was Gujarat chief minister.In April this year, PM Modi met the SRCC governing body and a delegation from the college at his residence to mark the institution's centenary. He also released a special commemorative postage stamp on the occasion.Established in 1926, SRCC has completed 100 years and has produced scholars, professionals, entrepreneurs, policymakers and leaders across different fields.

World.title: Traffic curbs in Kochi in view of police marathon
World.content:
Traffic restrictions will be in place in parts of the city on Sunday evening (September 6) in view of the Statewide marathon ahead of the Kerala Police Sports Meet, the Kochi City police said on Saturday (September 5).

Curbs will be imposed on the stretch of NH 544 between SCMS, Kalamassery, and JLN Stadium, Kaloor; Aluva-Ernakulam PWD Road, and the premises of the stadium between 3 p.m. and 7 p.m. The police have urged the public to cooperate and use alternative roads to avoid congestions.

World.title: 342 complete training at OTA; commissioned as officers in Indian Army
World.content:
Homemaker Rigzin Ladol and her retired teacher and husband Tundup Tsering from Zanskar district of the Union territory of Ladakh stood proudly next to their 24-year-old daughter Stanzin Tsangyang at the Officers Training Academy (OTA) in Chennai on Saturday morning. Their daughter had completed her training and was commissioned into the Army as a Lieutenant.

Lt. Stanzin Tsangyang was among the 342 persons who completed their training and were commissioned as officers during the Passing Out Parade (POP) at the OTA. “I was interested in sports, and I was in the NCC during my college days. I was interested in joining the Army,” says the engineering graduate. “She is the first from my family to join the Army,” says her father Mr. Tsering.

Like Ms. Tsangyang, Lt. Ritika Dubey from Gorakhpur in Uttar Pradesh is the first from her family to join the Armed forces. There were also Lieutenants Mohit Arora, Prashant Gurung, and M.R. Raswanth, who had followed their family’s tradition of serving in the Army. Besides, 17 cadets from friendly foreign countries such as Bhutan, Eswatini, Lesotho, Seychelles, Tanzania, Uganda, and Zimbabwe also completed their training on Saturday.

Earlier in the day, Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, Chief of the Naval Staff, reviewed the parade in Parameswaran Drill Square. During his speech, Mr. Swaminathan said: “Courage is a muscle. It strengthens every time you use it. Whether physical or moral, courage more often than not, means the ability to stand alone to your convictions. It cannot be downloaded in a crisis; it is built and engrained over time in the small choices we make every day.”

The character of warfare might have changed in many ways but fundamentally, war remained a profoundly human endeavour, said the Chief of the Naval Staff. “Combat operations may see new weapons being used across new domains, but their outcomes shall continue to be determined by the men and women who fight, lead, inspire, persist, and persevere.”

He presented the prestigious ‘Sword of Honour’ and Bronze Medal to Battalion Under Officer Gurkeerat Singh Hora, OTA Gold Medal to Academy Under Officer Abhinab Chauhan, and Silver Medal to Academy Cadet Adjutant Niket Singh Tomar.

World.title: China to proceed with Brahmaputra mega dam despite new concerns
World.content:
Fresh concerns triggered by the devastating glacial collapse along the Nepal-China border are unlikely to sway Beijing's plans to go ahead with the construction of a mega dam on the lower reaches of the Yarlung Zangbo, or the Brahmaputra River, in a seismically active region in Tibet near the border with India.

On July 23, 2026, a month before the August 26 flash flood and mudslides, China released its 15th Five-Year Plan for renewable energy, which called for advancing the construction of major projects, including the Yarlung Zangbo Lower Reaches Hydropower Project, as the mega dam project is referred to in China.

Underscoring the importance accorded to the plan, China’s Vice Premier Zhang Guoqing visited Nyingchi in Tibet, near the border, in April this year. "We must shoulder the principal responsibility for project‑building and build this landmark mega project of the new era,” he was quoted as saying, adding that the government would “put quality first, safety as the foundation, strictly enforce construction standards and ecological‑environmental‑protection requirements, and keep construction progress subordinate to quality and safety.”

‘Project of the century’

At a groundbreaking ceremony in July 2025, China’s second-ranked leader and Premier Li Qiang, who travelled to Nyingchi, announced the start of construction of what he called “the project of the century”. A total investment of 1.2 trillion Yuan (around ₹14 lakh crore) was announced for the construction of five power stations.

Since then, there has been little public information about the project, although Mr. Zhang’s visit this year shed some light on how the project will go forward, including the setting up of the new State-run China Yajiang Group to run the entire project, which he inspected.

China has already opened one major dam on the middle reaches of the Yarlung Zangbo at Zangmu. A State media report earlier this month lauded the construction of the dam, saying it had “provided a solution to nearly 26 percent of electricity demand in Southwest China’s Xizang [Tibet] Autonomous Region”, the report said, detailing an elaborate “fishway” designed to help fish move between upstream and downstream sections. The report quoted design engineer Zhang Lianming as saying the fishway would likely be used for future projects.

In June this year, a “final acceptance meeting” of the Zangmu project was held, declaring that the dam, which started construction in 2010, had generated 22.2 billion kilowatt-hours of energy “equivalent to saving approximately 7.4 million tonnes of standard coal and cutting carbon dioxide emissions by around 22.2 million tonnes”.

The energy generation of the new project near the India border, where the course of the Yarlung Zangbo stunningly falls over the “great bend” and turns towards India, is expected to easily dwarf Zangmu.

While there have been no official projections, Chinese analysts project 60 GW installed capacity and 300 billion kilowatt-hours of power a year, more than three times the Three Gorges.

While the project has been described as a “run-of-the-river” dam, it will also involve the construction of a reservoir. This is likely to be located in the town of Mainling, upstream of Nyingchi, a prefecture-level city that is also home to a key airport, according to an analysis published on Wednesday by David Fishman, a Shanghai-based analyst writing on energy who looked at reports of relocations to ascertain the likely location. The water will be diverted at the top of the great bend into an approximately 40-km-long tunnel, Mr. Fishman wrote on his Substack, “Crossing the River”, as its descending force powers five 12-GW powerhouses before rejoining the river.

India’s concerns

Of concern to India is how much water is likely to be stored in the reservoir and how the tunnel will affect downstream flows, as well as possible broader ecological impacts. The lack of information has posed an obstacle in assessing the possible impact.

Later this month, India and China will hold a meeting of the Expert-Level Mechanism on Trans-border Rivers. However, the sharing of hydrological data, officials say, has not been regular and has on occasion been suspended during difficult periods in relations.

Asked about the project, China’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said last year that Beijing “always maintained a highly responsible attitude toward transboundary river development and has rich experience in hydropower project development”. He said the “construction of the project is beneficial for disaster prevention and mitigation throughout the entire river basin and will not have adverse effects on downstream areas”.

“China has conducted hydrological reporting, flood control, and disaster reduction cooperation with relevant downstream countries and has also engaged in necessary communication regarding the project,” he said.
